bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通-{鑑}-第086巻

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror to Aid in Governance, Volume 86.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 86.

sentences.zh: 【晉紀八】起旃蒙赤奮若，盡著雍執徐，凡四年。

translations.literal: [Jin Annals 8] Beginning from Zhanmeng Chifenruo, ending at Zhuoyong Zhixu—in all, four years.
translations.idiomatic: [Jin Annals 8] From Zhanmeng Chifenruo through Zhuoyong Zhixu—four years in all.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，張方廢羊-{后}-。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Zhang Fang deposed Empress Yang.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, Zhang Fang deposed Empress Yang.

sentences.zh: -{游}-楷等攻皇甫重，累年不能克，重遣其養子昌求救-{於}-外。

translations.literal: You Kai and others attacked Huangfu Chong; for years they could not overcome him. Chong sent his adopted son Chang to seek rescue from outside.
translations.idiomatic: You Kai and others besieged Huangfu Chong for years without taking him; Chong sent his adopted son Chang to seek help from outside.

sentences.zh: 昌詣司空越，越以太宰顒新與山東連和，不肯出兵。

translations.literal: Chang went to see the Minister over the Masses Yue; Yue, because the Grand Marshal Yong had newly allied with the east, refused to send troops.
translations.idiomatic: Chang went to the Minister over the Masses Yue, but Yue—since Grand Marshal Yong had just allied with the eastern provinces—refused to march.

sentences.zh: 昌乃與故殿中人楊篇詐稱越命，迎羊-{后}--{於}-金墉城。

translations.literal: Chang then, with the former palace attendant Yang Pian, falsely claimed Yue's order and welcomed Empress Yang from Jinyong fortress.
translations.idiomatic: Chang then conspired with the former palace attendant Yang Pian to forge Yue's orders and escort Empress Yang from Jinyong fortress.

sentences.zh: 入宮，以-{后}-令-{發}-兵討張方，奉迎大駕。

translations.literal: Entering the palace, he used the empress's command to raise troops to attack Zhang Fang and to welcome back the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Once inside the palace, he invoked the empress's authority to mobilize troops against Zhang Fang and restore the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 事起倉猝，百官初皆從之；

translations.literal: The affair arose in sudden haste; at first all the officials followed it;
translations.idiomatic: The plot erupted suddenly; at first all the officials went along;

sentences.zh: 俄知其詐，相與誅昌。

translations.literal: before long they knew it was a fraud and together executed Chang.
translations.idiomatic: before long they learned it was a fraud and together put Chang to death.

sentences.zh: 顒請遣-{御}-史宣詔喩重令降，重不奉詔。

translations.literal: Yong requested that an imperial censor be sent to proclaim an edict instructing Chong to surrender; Chong did not accept the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Yong asked that an imperial censor proclaim an edict urging Chong to surrender, but Chong refused to comply.

sentences.zh: 先是城中不知長沙厲王及皇甫商已死，重獲-{御}-史騶人，問曰：「我弟將兵來，欲至未？」

translations.literal: Earlier the city had not known that the Prince of Changsha and Huangfu Shang were already dead. Chong captured an imperial censor's groom and asked, "My younger brother is leading troops here—has he arrived yet?"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the garrison had not known that the Prince of Changsha and Huangfu Shang were already dead. Chong seized an imperial censor's groom and asked, "My brother is marching to relieve us—has he arrived?"

sentences.zh: 騶人曰：「已爲河間王所害。」

translations.literal: The groom said, "He has already been killed by the Prince of Hejian."
translations.idiomatic: The groom replied, "He was already killed by the Prince of Hejian."

sentences.zh: 重失色，立殺騶人。

translations.literal: Chong turned pale and immediately killed the groom.
translations.idiomatic: Chong went pale and at once killed the groom.

sentences.zh: -{於}-是城中知無外救，共殺重以降。

translations.literal: Thereupon the city knew there was no outside rescue; together they killed Chong and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Then the city realized no relief was coming; the garrison killed Chong together and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 顒以馮翊太守張輔爲秦州刺史。

translations.literal: Yong appointed Fengyi Administrator Zhang Fu as Inspector of Qin province.
translations.idiomatic: Yong appointed Zhang Fu, administrator of Fengyi, inspector of Qin province.

sentences.zh: 六月，甲子，安-{豐}-元侯王戎薨-{於}-郟。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on jiazi, Marquis Yuan of Anfeng Wang Rong died at Jia.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jiazi, Wang Rong, Marquis Yuan of Anfeng, died at Jia.

sentences.zh: 張輔至秦州，殺天水太守封尚，欲以立威；

translations.literal: When Zhang Fu reached Qin province, he killed Tianshui Administrator Feng Shang, intending thereby to establish his authority;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Fu reached Qin province, he killed Feng Shang, administrator of Tianshui, hoping to cow the region;

sentences.zh: 又召隴西太守韓稚，稚子-{樸}-勒兵撃輔。

translations.literal: he also summoned Longxi Administrator Han Zhi; Zhi's son Pu led troops to attack Fu.
translations.idiomatic: he also summoned Han Zhi, administrator of Longxi; Zhi's son Pu raised troops and struck at Fu.

sentences.zh: 輔軍敗，死。

translations.literal: Fu's army was defeated and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's army was routed and he was killed.

sentences.zh: 涼州司馬楊胤言-{於}-張軌曰：「韓稚擅殺刺史，明公杖鉞一方，不可以不討。」

translations.literal: Liang province Marshal Yang Yin said to Zhang Gui: "Han Zhi on his own authority killed the inspector; my lord holds the imperial baton in this region—you cannot fail to punish him."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yin, marshal of Liang province, said to Zhang Gui, "Han Zhi murdered the inspector on his own authority. You command this region with the imperial baton—you cannot let that pass unpunished."

sentences.zh: 軌從之，遣中督護汜瑗帥衆二萬討稚，稚詣軌降。

translations.literal: Gui agreed and sent Central Commandant Si Yuan leading twenty thousand men to attack Zhi; Zhi came to Gui and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Gui agreed, sent Central Commandant Si Yuan with twenty thousand men against Zhi, and Zhi came to Gui and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 未-{幾}-，鮮卑若羅拔能寇涼州，軌遣司馬宋配撃之，斬拔能，俘十-{餘}-萬口，威名大振。

translations.literal: Before long the Xianbei chief Luoboneng raided Liang province; Gui sent Marshal Song Pei to attack him, beheaded Luoboneng, and captured more than a hundred thousand people—his fame shook the land.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Xianbei chief Luoboneng raided Liang province. Gui sent Marshal Song Pei against him; Song beheaded Luoboneng, took more than a hundred thousand captives, and Gui's renown soared.

sentences.zh: 漢王淵攻東贏公騰，騰-{復}-乞師-{於}-拓跋猗迤，衞操勸猗迤助之。

translations.literal: Han King Yuan attacked Duke Teng of Dongying; Teng again begged troops from the Tuoba chief Yituo, and Wei Cao urged Yituo to aid him.
translations.idiomatic: Han King Yuan attacked Duke Teng of Dongying. Teng again begged the Tuoba chief Yituo for troops, and Wei Cao urged Yituo to help.

sentences.zh: 猗迤帥輕騎數千救騰，斬漢將綦毋豚。

translations.literal: Yituo led several thousand light horsemen to rescue Teng and beheaded the Han general Qimu Tun.
translations.idiomatic: Yituo led several thousand light cavalry to relieve Teng and slew the Han general Qimu Tun.

sentences.zh: 詔假猗迤大單-{于}-，加操右將軍。

translations.literal: An edict provisionally appointed Yituo Great Chanyu and promoted Cao to General of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: An edict provisionally made Yituo Great Chanyu and promoted Cao to General of the Right.

sentences.zh: 甲申，猗迤卒，子普根代立。

translations.literal: On jiashen, Yituo died; his son Pugen succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, Yituo died and his son Pugen succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 東海中尉劉洽以張方劫遷車駕，勸司空越起兵討之。

translations.literal: Donghai Commandant Liu Qia, because Zhang Fang had seized and moved the imperial carriage, urged the Minister over the Masses Yue to raise troops and attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qia, commandant of Donghai, urged Minister over the Masses Yue to raise troops against Zhang Fang for having seized and moved the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，越傳檄山東-{征}-、鎭、州、郡-{云}-：「欲糾帥義旅，奉迎天子，還-{復}-舊都。」

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Yue circulated a proclamation through the eastern provinces, garrisons, prefectures, and commanderies, saying: "We wish to gather righteous armies, welcome the Son of Heaven, and restore the old capital."
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Yue sent a proclamation through the eastern provinces: "We mean to gather righteous armies, receive the Son of Heaven back, and restore the old capital."

sentences.zh: 東平王楙聞之，懼；

translations.literal: The Prince of Dongping Mao heard this and was afraid;
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Dongping Mao heard this, he was afraid;

sentences.zh: 長史王修説楙曰：「東海，宗室重望；

translations.literal: Chief Administrator Wang Xiu advised Mao: "The Prince of Donghai enjoys great standing among the imperial house;
translations.idiomatic: Chief Administrator Wang Xiu advised Mao, "The Prince of Donghai enjoys great standing in the imperial house;

sentences.zh: 今興義兵，公宜舉徐州以授之，則免-{於}-難，且有克讓之美矣。」

translations.literal: now that he is raising righteous troops, you ought to yield Xu province to him—then you escape disaster and gain credit for gracious yielding."
translations.idiomatic: now that he is raising righteous troops, you should yield Xu province to him—you will escape disaster and win credit for gracious yielding."

sentences.zh: 楙從之。

translations.literal: Mao followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Mao took his advice.

sentences.zh: 越乃以司空領徐州都督，楙自爲兗州刺史；

translations.literal: Yue then held the title of Minister over the Masses while also serving as Regional Commander of Xu province; Mao made himself Inspector of Yan province;
translations.idiomatic: Yue then served as Minister over the Masses and regional commander of Xu province; Mao made himself inspector of Yan province;

sentences.zh: 詔卽遣使者劉虔授之。

translations.literal: the court immediately sent the envoy Liu Qian to invest them.
translations.idiomatic: the court at once sent the envoy Liu Qian to confirm the appointments.

sentences.zh: 是時，越兄弟-{並}--{據}-方任，-{於}-是-{范}-陽王虓及王浚等共推越爲盟主，越輒選置刺史以下，朝士多赴之。

translations.literal: At this time Yue's brothers together held regional appointments; thereupon the Prince of Fanyang Xiao and Wang Jun and others jointly acclaimed Yue as alliance leader, and Yue at will appointed people to posts below inspector—many court officials joined him.
translations.idiomatic: By then Yue's brothers together held regional posts; the Prince of Fanyang Xiao, Wang Jun, and others jointly made Yue alliance leader, and Yue appointed officials down to the rank of inspector as he saw fit—many courtiers flocked to him.

sentences.zh: 成都王穎旣廢，河北人多憐之。

translations.literal: After the Prince of Chengdu Ying had been deposed, many people north of the Yellow River pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: After Prince of Chengdu Ying was deposed, many north of the Yellow River pitied him.

sentences.zh: 穎故將公師籓等自稱將軍，起兵-{於}-趙、魏，衆至數萬。

translations.literal: Ying's former generals Gongshi Fan and others styled themselves generals and raised troops in Zhao and Wei—their numbers reached tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's former generals Gongshi Fan and others declared themselves generals and raised troops in Zhao and Wei; their forces soon numbered tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 初，上黨武鄕羯人石勒，有膽力，善騎射。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Jie man Shi Le of Wuxiang in Shangdang had courage and strength and was skilled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Jie tribesman Shi Le of Wuxiang in Shangdang was bold and strong and excelled at mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 并州大饑，建威將軍閻粹説東嬴公騰執諸胡-{於}-山東，賣充軍實。

translations.literal: A great famine struck Bing province; General of Establishing Prestige Yan Cui urged Duke Teng of Dongying to seize all the Hu peoples east of the mountains and sell them to fill the army's stores.
translations.idiomatic: A great famine struck Bing province. General of Establishing Prestige Yan Cui urged Duke Teng of Dongying to seize the non-Han peoples east of the mountains and sell them to fill the army's stores.

sentences.zh: 勒亦被掠，賣爲茌平人師懽奴，懽奇其狀貌而免之。

translations.literal: Le was also taken; he was sold as a slave to Shi Huan of Chiping—Huan marveled at his appearance and spared him.
translations.idiomatic: Le was seized too and sold as a slave to Shi Huan of Chiping; Huan was struck by his looks and spared him.

sentences.zh: 懽家鄰-{於}-馬牧，勒乃與牧帥汲桑結壯士爲群盜。

translations.literal: Huan's home lay near horse pastures; Le then joined herd chief Ji Sang and formed a band of stalwart men as robbers.
translations.idiomatic: Huan's home lay near the horse pastures; Le joined the herd chief Ji Sang and with stalwart companions became bandits.

sentences.zh: 及公師籓起，桑與勒帥數百騎赴之。

translations.literal: When Gongshi Fan rose, Sang and Le led several hundred horsemen to join him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gongshi Fan rose, Sang and Le led several hundred horsemen to his banner.

sentences.zh: 桑始命勒以石爲姓，勒爲名。

translations.literal: Sang first ordered him to take the surname Shi and the personal name Le.
translations.idiomatic: Sang first gave him the surname Shi and the personal name Le.

sentences.zh: 籓攻陷郡縣，殺二千石、長史，轉前，攻鄴。

translations.literal: Fan seized commanderies and counties, killed prefects of two thousand dan and chief administrators, advanced forward, and attacked Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Fan overran commanderies and counties, killed prefects and chief administrators, and pressed on to attack Ye.

sentences.zh: 平昌公模甚懼；

translations.literal: Duke of Pingchang Mo was deeply afraid;
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Pingchang Mo was deeply alarmed;

sentences.zh: -{范}-陽王虓遣其將苟晞救鄴，與廣平太守譙國丁紹共撃籓，走之。

translations.literal: the Prince of Fanyang Xiao sent his general Gou Xi to rescue Ye; together with Guangping Administrator Ding Shao of Qiao they attacked Fan and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: the Prince of Fanyang Xiao sent his general Gou Xi to relieve Ye; with Guangping Administrator Ding Shao of Qiao he attacked Fan and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 八月，辛-{丑}-，大赦。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on xinchou, a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on xinchou, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 司空越以琅邪王睿爲平東將軍，監徐州諸軍事，留守下邳。

translations.literal: The Minister over the Masses Yue appointed the Prince of Langye Rui as General Who Pacifies the East, overseeing Xu province military affairs, stationed at Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: Minister over the Masses Yue appointed Prince of Langye Rui General Who Pacifies the East, put him in charge of Xu province forces, and left him at Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 睿請王導爲司馬，委以軍事。

translations.literal: Rui requested Wang Dao as Marshal and entrusted him with military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Rui asked for Wang Dao as marshal and entrusted him with military affairs.

sentences.zh: 越帥甲士三萬，西屯蕭縣，-{范}-陽王虓自許屯-{於}-滎陽。

translations.literal: Yue led thirty thousand armored troops west to encamp at Xiao county; the Prince of Fanyang Xiao himself, from Xu, encamped at Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yue led thirty thousand armored troops west to Xiao county; the Prince of Fanyang Xiao marched from Xu and encamped at Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 越承-{製}-以豫州刺史劉喬爲冀州刺史，以-{范}-陽王虓領豫州刺史；

translations.literal: Yue, acting on imperial authority, appointed Liu Qiao of Yuzhou as Inspector of Ji province and had the Prince of Fanyang Xiao take charge of Yuzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Acting on imperial authority, Yue made Liu Qiao of Yuzhou inspector of Ji province and had the Prince of Fanyang Xiao take charge of Yuzhou;

sentences.zh: 喬以虓非天子命，-{發}-兵拒之。

translations.literal: Qiao said Xiao lacked the Son of Heaven's appointment and raised troops to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao said Xiao lacked the Son of Heaven's appointment and raised troops to resist him.

sentences.zh: 虓以劉琨爲司馬，越以劉蕃爲淮北護軍，劉輿爲穎川太守。

translations.literal: Xiao made Liu Kun his Marshal; Yue appointed Liu Fan as Protector of the Army north of the Huai and Liu Yu as Administrator of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao made Liu Kun his marshal; Yue appointed Liu Fan protector of the army north of the Huai and Liu Yu administrator of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 喬上尚書，列輿兄弟罪惡，因引兵攻許，遣其長子祐將兵拒越-{於}-蕭縣之靈壁，越兵不能進。

translations.literal: Qiao memorialized the Ministry of Works listing the crimes of the Yu brothers and led troops to attack Xu; he sent his eldest son You with troops to block Yue at Lingbi in Xiao county—Yue's army could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao memorialized the Ministry of Works listing the Yu brothers' crimes, then marched on Xu; he sent his eldest son You to block Yue at Lingbi in Xiao county, and Yue's army could not advance.

sentences.zh: 東平王楙在兗州，-{徴}-求不已，郡縣不堪命。

translations.literal: The Prince of Dongping Mao was in Yan province, demanding levies without end; the commanderies and counties could not bear the burden.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Dongping Mao was in Yan province, levying demands without end; commanderies and counties could not endure it.

sentences.zh: -{范}-陽王虓遣苟晞還兗州，徙楙都督靑州。

translations.literal: the Prince of Fanyang Xiao sent Gou Xi back to Yan province and moved Mao to be Regional Commander of Qing province.
translations.idiomatic: the Prince of Fanyang Xiao sent Gou Xi back to Yan province and transferred Mao to be regional commander of Qing province.

sentences.zh: 楙不受命，背山東諸侯，與劉喬合。

translations.literal: Mao would not accept the order; he turned his back on the eastern lords and allied with Liu Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Mao refused the order, broke with the eastern lords, and allied with Liu Qiao.

sentences.zh: 太宰顒聞山東兵起，甚懼。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Yong heard that troops had risen in the east and was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Marshal Yong heard that the eastern provinces had risen in arms, he was deeply alarmed.

sentences.zh: 以公師籓爲成都王穎起兵，壬午，表穎爲鎭軍大將軍、都督河北諸軍事，給兵千人；

translations.literal: Learning that Gongshi Fan was raising troops for the Prince of Chengdu Ying, on renwu he memorialized making Ying General of Garrisoning the Army and Commander-in-chief of Hebei military affairs, granting a thousand troops;
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Gongshi Fan was raising troops for Prince of Chengdu Ying, on renwu he memorialized making Ying General of Garrisoning the Army and commander-in-chief of Hebei forces, with a thousand troops;

sentences.zh: 以盧-{志}-爲魏郡太守，隨穎鎭鄴，欲以撫安之；

translations.literal: he appointed Lu Zhi Administrator of Wei commandery to accompany Ying in garrisoning Ye, intending thereby to reassure the region;
translations.idiomatic: he appointed Lu Zhi administrator of Wei commandery to accompany Ying at Ye, hoping to pacify the north;

sentences.zh: 又遣建武將軍呂朗屯洛陽。

translations.literal: he also sent General of Establishing Martial Lu Lang to garrison Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: he also sent General of Establishing Martial Lu Lang to garrison Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 顒-{發}-詔，令東海王越等各就國，越等不從。

translations.literal: Yong issued an edict ordering each of the Prince of Donghai Yue and the others to return to their states; Yue and the others did not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Yong issued an edict ordering the Prince of Donghai Yue and the others each to return to his fief; Yue and the others refused.

sentences.zh: 會得劉喬上事，冬，十月，丙子，下詔稱：「劉輿迫脅-{范}-陽王虓，造構凶逆。

translations.literal: When Liu Qiao's memorial arrived, in winter, the tenth month, on bingzi, an edict declared: "Liu Yu coerced the Prince of Fanyang Xiao and contrived vicious treason.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Qiao's memorial arrived, in winter, the tenth month, on bingzi, an edict declared, "Liu Yu coerced the Prince of Fanyang Xiao and contrived vicious treason.

sentences.zh: 其令鎭南大將軍劉弘、平南將軍彭城王釋、-{征}-東大將軍劉准，各勒所統，與劉喬-{並}-力；

translations.literal: Let General Who Guards the South Liu Hong, General Who Pacifies the South Prince of Pengcheng Shi, and General Who Expedites the East Liu Zhun each lead their forces and join Liu Qiao in concert;
translations.idiomatic: Let General Who Guards the South Liu Hong, General Who Pacifies the South Prince of Pengcheng Shi, and General Who Expedites the East Liu Zhun each lead their forces and join Liu Qiao in concert;

sentences.zh: 以張方爲大都督，統精卒十萬，與呂朗共會許昌，誅輿兄弟。」

translations.literal: appoint Zhang Fang Grand Commander-in-chief with a hundred thousand elite troops to join Lu Lang at Xuchang and execute the Yu brothers."
translations.idiomatic: appoint Zhang Fang grand commander-in-chief with a hundred thousand elite troops to join Lu Lang at Xuchang and execute the Yu brothers."

sentences.zh: 釋，宣帝弟子穆王權之孫也。

translations.literal: Shi was the grandson of Prince Mu, younger brother of Emperor Xuan's son Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was the grandson of Prince Mu, son of Emperor Xuan's younger brother Quan.

sentences.zh: 丁-{丑}-，顒使成都王穎領將軍樓褒等，前車騎將軍石超領北中郎將王闡等，-{據}-河橋，爲劉喬繼援。

translations.literal: On dingchou, Yong sent the Prince of Chengdu Ying leading General Lou Bao and others, and Former General of Chariots and Cavalry Shi Chao leading Northern Gentlemen's General Wang Chan and others, to hold the Yellow River bridge as follow-on aid for Liu Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, Yong sent Prince of Chengdu Ying with General Lou Bao and others, and Former General of Chariots and Cavalry Shi Chao with Northern Gentlemen's General Wang Chan and others, to hold the Yellow River bridge as follow-on support for Liu Qiao.

sentences.zh: 進喬鎭東將軍，假節。

translations.literal: Qiao was promoted to General Who Pacifies the East, with provisional credentials.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao was promoted to General Who Pacifies the East and given provisional credentials.

sentences.zh: 劉弘遺喬及司空越書，欲使之解怨釋兵，同獎王室，皆不-{聽}-。

translations.literal: Liu Hong sent letters to Qiao and to the Minister over the Masses Yue, wishing them to lay aside enmity and raise arms together to reward the royal house—neither would listen.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong wrote to Qiao and to Minister over the Masses Yue, urging them to lay down their feud and take up arms together for the royal house—neither would listen.

sentences.zh: 弘又上表曰：「自頃兵戈紛亂，猜禍鋒生，疑隙構-{於}-群王，災難延-{於}-宗子。

translations.literal: Hong also submitted a memorial saying: "Recently arms have risen in chaos and suspicion and disaster have flashed among us; mistrust has been built up among the princes and calamity has spread to the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Hong also submitted a memorial: "Lately arms have risen in chaos; suspicion and disaster flash among us; mistrust has grown among the princes and calamity has spread through the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 今夕爲忠，明旦爲逆，翩其反而，互爲戎首。

translations.literal: Tonight one is loyal, tomorrow rebellious—they whirl about and turn on each other, each becoming leader of the war.
translations.idiomatic: Tonight one is loyal, tomorrow a rebel—they whirl about and turn on each other, each becoming a war leader.

sentences.zh: 載籍以來，骨肉之禍未有如今者也，臣竊悲之！

translations.literal: In all the records, there has never been such trouble among kin as now—I grieve at it in private!
translations.idiomatic: In all the records there has never been such strife among kin as now—I grieve for it in private!

sentences.zh: 今邊陲無備豫之儲，中華有杼軸之困，而股肱之臣，不惟國體，職競尋常，自相楚剝。

translations.literal: Now the frontiers lack stores for unexpected need; the heartland suffers the distress of the loom's axle; yet the limbs of state do not consider the nation's body—they compete in the ordinary way and flay one another.
translations.idiomatic: The frontiers lack stores against sudden need; the heartland suffers the strain of the loom's axle; yet the state's chief servants do not consider the nation's welfare—they compete in petty ways and flay one another.

sentences.zh: 萬一四夷乘虚爲變，此亦猛虎交鬪自效-{於}-卞莊者矣。

translations.literal: Should the four barbarians on some empty pretext make trouble, this too would be tigers fighting for the profit of Bian Zhuangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Should the four barbarians seize the moment to make trouble, this would be like two tigers fighting while Bian Zhuangzi waits to strike both.

sentences.zh: 臣以爲宜速-{發}-明詔詔越等，令兩釋猜嫌，各保分局。

translations.literal: I think we should quickly issue a clear edict calling Yue and the others to release their suspicions and each keep to his territory.
translations.idiomatic: I believe a clear edict should quickly be sent to Yue and the others, ordering them to lay aside suspicion and each keep to his territory.

sentences.zh: 自今以-{後}-，其有不被詔書，擅興兵馬者，天下共伐之。」

translations.literal: From now on, whoever without imperial edict on his own authority raises troops—the realm together shall attack him."
translations.idiomatic: From now on, whoever raises troops without imperial edict—the realm together shall attack him."

sentences.zh: 時太宰顒方拒關東，倚喬爲助，不納其言。

translations.literal: At that time Grand Marshal Yong was blocking the east and leaning on Qiao as support—he did not accept these words.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Grand Marshal Yong was holding off the east and leaning on Qiao for support; he would not heed these words.

sentences.zh: 喬乘虚襲許，破之。

translations.literal: Qiao seized the moment and raided Xu, breaking it.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao seized the moment, raided Xu, and took it.

sentences.zh: 劉琨將兵救許，不及，遂與兄輿及-{范}-陽王虓倶奔河北；

translations.literal: Liu Kun led troops to rescue Xu but did not arrive in time; he fled with his brother Yu and the Prince of Fanyang Xiao together to Hebei;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun marched to relieve Xu but arrived too late; he fled with his brother Yu and the Prince of Fanyang Xiao to Hebei;

sentences.zh: 琨父母爲喬所執。

translations.literal: Kun's parents were seized by Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao seized Kun's parents.

sentences.zh: 劉弘以張方殘暴，知顒必敗，乃遣參軍劉盤爲督護，帥諸軍受司空越節度。

translations.literal: Liu Hong, considering Zhang Fang brutal and knowing Yong would surely fall, sent Military Adviser Liu Pan as Commandant Protector leading all armies to accept the Minister over the Masses Yue's direction.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong, seeing Zhang Fang's brutality and knowing Yong would fall, sent his military adviser Liu Pan as commandant protector to lead his forces under Minister over the Masses Yue's command.

sentences.zh: 時天下大亂，弘專督江、漢，威行南服。

translations.literal: The realm was in great disorder; Hong alone supervised the Yangtze and Han, his prestige prevailing in the south.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was in chaos; Hong alone governed the Yangtze and Han, and his authority held sway in the south.

sentences.zh: 謀事有成者，則曰「某人之功」；

translations.literal: When a plan succeeded he would say, "So-and-so's achievement";
translations.idiomatic: When a plan succeeded he would say, "That was so-and-so's achievement";

sentences.zh: 如有負敗，則曰「老子之罪」。

translations.literal: if there was failure he would say, "This old man's fault."
translations.idiomatic: if there was failure he would say, "This old man's fault."

sentences.zh: 毎有興-{發}-，手書守相，丁-{寧}-款密。

translations.literal: Whenever he undertook a campaign he personally wrote the district governors, urgent and full of care.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he undertook a campaign he personally wrote the district governors, earnest and meticulous.

sentences.zh: 所以人皆感悅，急赴之，-{咸}-曰：「得劉公一紙書，賢-{於}-十部從事。」

translations.literal: Therefore everyone was moved and eager to serve—they all said, "A single letter from Duke Liu is worth more than ten staff officers."
translations.idiomatic: Everyone was moved and eager to serve; they said, "One letter from Duke Liu is worth more than ten staff officers."

sentences.zh: 前廣漢太守辛冉説弘以從橫之事，弘怒，斬之。

translations.literal: The former Administrator of Guanghan Xin Ran urged Hong toward alliance tactics; Hong was angry and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Former administrator of Guanghan Xin Ran urged Hong toward alliance politics; Hong was enraged and executed him.

sentences.zh: 有星孛-{於}-北-{斗}-。

translations.literal: A comet appeared at the Northern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: A comet appeared at the Northern Dipper.

sentences.zh: 平昌公模遣將軍宋冑趣河橋。

translations.literal: Duke of Pingchang Mo sent General Song Zhou to hurry to the Yellow River bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Pingchang Mo sent General Song Zhou to hurry to the Yellow River bridge.

sentences.zh: 十一月，立節將軍周權，詐被檄，自稱平西將軍，-{復}-立羊-{后}-。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, General Who Establishes Integrity Zhou Quan, falsely claiming to have received an edict, styled himself General Who Pacifies the West and again installed Empress Yang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, General Who Establishes Integrity Zhou Quan, falsely claiming an edict, styled himself General Who Pacifies the West and restored Empress Yang.

sentences.zh: 洛陽令何喬攻權，殺之，-{復}-廢羊-{后}-。

translations.literal: Luoyang Magistrate He Qiao attacked Quan, killed him, and again deposed Empress Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang magistrate He Qiao attacked Quan, killed him, and again deposed Empress Yang.

sentences.zh: 太宰顒矯詔，以羊-{后}-屢爲-{姦}-人所立，遣尚書田淑敕留-{臺}-賜-{後}-死。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Yong forged an edict saying that because Empress Yang had repeatedly been installed by treacherous men, he sent Minister of Writs Tian Shu with orders to detain her at the capital and grant her death.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Yong forged an edict, claiming Empress Yang had repeatedly been installed by traitors, and sent Minister of Writs Tian Shu to detain her at the capital and order her death.

sentences.zh: 詔書累至，司隸校尉劉暾等上奏，固執以爲：「羊庶人門戸殘破，廢放空宮，門禁峻密，無縁得與-{姦}-人構亂。

translations.literal: The edicts piled up; Director of Retainers Liu Dun and others submitted memorials insisting: "The commoner Yang's household is broken, she is deposed and lodged in an empty palace, the gates strictly sealed—she could not have colluded with treacherous men to stir disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Edict after edict arrived; Director of Retainers Liu Dun and others memorialized, insisting, "The deposed Lady Yang's household is ruined; she is confined in an empty palace under strict guard—she could not have colluded with traitors.

sentences.zh: 衆無愚智，皆謂其冤。

translations.literal: High and low, wise and foolish—all say she was wronged.
translations.idiomatic: High and low alike say she was wronged.

sentences.zh: 今殺一枯窮之人，而令天下傷慘，何益-{於}-治！」

translations.literal: To kill one withered helpless person and make the realm mourn—what benefit for governance!"
translations.idiomatic: To kill one helpless, ruined woman and fill the realm with grief—what good is that for governance?"

sentences.zh: 顒怒，遣呂朗收暾。

translations.literal: Yong was angry and sent Lu Lang to arrest Dun.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was enraged and sent Lu Lang to arrest Dun.

sentences.zh: 暾奔靑州，依髙密王略。

translations.literal: Dun fled to Qing province and relied on Prince of Gaomi Lüe.
translations.idiomatic: Dun fled to Qing province and took refuge with Prince of Gaomi Lüe.

sentences.zh: 然羊-{后}-亦以是得免。

translations.literal: Yet Empress Yang was spared because of this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Empress Yang was spared because of this.

sentences.zh: 十二月，呂朗等東屯滎陽，成都王穎進-{據}-洛陽。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Lu Lang and others encamped east at Xingyang; the Prince of Chengdu Ying advanced and held Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Lu Lang and others encamped east at Xingyang; Prince of Chengdu Ying advanced and occupied Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 劉琨説冀州刺史太原温羨，使讓位-{於}--{范}-陽王虓。

translations.literal: Liu Kun persuaded Inspector of Ji province Wen Xian of Taiyuan to yield his post to the Prince of Fanyang Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun persuaded Wen Xian of Taiyuan, inspector of Ji province, to yield his post to the Prince of Fanyang Xiao.

sentences.zh: 虓領冀州，遣琨詣幽州乞師-{於}-王浚；

translations.literal: Xiao took charge of Ji province and sent Kun to Youzhou to beg troops from Wang Jun;
translations.idiomatic: Xiao assumed control of Ji province and sent Liu Kun to Youzhou to request reinforcements from Wang Jun;

sentences.zh: 浚以突騎資之，撃王闡-{於}-河上，殺之。

translations.literal: Jun supplied him with shock cavalry, attacked Wang Chan on the river, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun furnished him with shock cavalry, attacked Wang Chan on the river, and slew him.

sentences.zh: 琨遂與虓引兵濟河，斬石超-{於}-滎陽。

translations.literal: Kun then, together with Xiao, led troops across the river and beheaded Shi Chao at Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Kun then joined Xiao in leading an army across the Yellow River and beheaded Shi Chao at Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 劉喬自考城引退。

translations.literal: Liu Qiao withdrew from Kaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qiao withdrew from Kaocheng.

sentences.zh: 虓遣琨及督護田徽東撃東平王楙-{於}-廩丘，楙走還國。

translations.literal: Xiao sent Kun and the supervisor of the guard Tian Hui east to attack the Prince of Dongping, Mao, at Linqiu; Mao fled back to his state.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao dispatched Liu Kun and the guard supervisor Tian Hui east to attack the Prince of Dongping, Mao, at Linqiu; Mao fled back to his fief.

sentences.zh: 琨、徽引兵東迎越，撃劉祐-{於}-譙；

translations.literal: Kun and Hui led troops east to welcome Yue and attacked Liu You at Qiao;
translations.idiomatic: Kun and Hui marched east to meet Sima Yue and attacked Liu You at Qiao;

sentences.zh: 祐敗死，喬衆遂潰，喬奔平氏。

translations.literal: You was defeated and died; Qiao's forces then collapsed, and Qiao fled to Pingshi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu You was defeated and killed; Qiao's army broke apart, and Qiao fled to Pingshi.

sentences.zh: 司空越進屯陽武，王浚遣其將祁弘帥突騎鮮卑、烏桓爲越先驅。

translations.literal: Minister over the Masses Yue advanced and encamped at Yangwu; Wang Jun sent his general Qi Hong to lead Xianbei and Wuhuan shock cavalry as Yue's vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Minister over the Masses Yue advanced and encamped at Yangwu; Wang Jun sent his general Qi Hong at the head of Xianbei and Wuhuan shock cavalry to serve as Yue's vanguard.

sentences.zh: 初，陳敏旣克石冰，自謂勇略無敵，有割-{據}-江東之-{志}-。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Chen Min had defeated Shi Bing, he considered himself unrivaled in courage and strategy and harbored the ambition to carve out and hold Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Chen Min had defeated Shi Bing, he believed himself unmatched in courage and strategy and set his heart on carving out and holding Jiangdong for himself.

sentences.zh: 其父怒曰：「滅我門者，必此兒也！」

translations.literal: His father said in anger, "The one who will destroy our house must be this boy!"
translations.idiomatic: His father said furiously, "The one who will destroy our house will surely be this boy!"

sentences.zh: 遂以憂卒。

translations.literal: He then died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: He then died of grief.

sentences.zh: 敏以喪去職。

translations.literal: Min left office on account of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Min resigned his post to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 司空越起敏爲右將軍、前鋒都督。

translations.literal: Minister over the Masses Yue recalled Min and appointed him Right General and Vanguard Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Minister over the Masses Yue recalled Min and made him Right General and Vanguard Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 越爲劉祐所敗，敏請東歸收兵，遂-{據}--{歴}-陽叛。

translations.literal: When Yue was defeated by Liu You, Min asked to return east to gather troops and then seized Liyang and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue was defeated by Liu You, Min asked leave to return east and raise troops; he then seized Liyang and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 呉王常侍甘卓，棄宮東歸，至-{歴}-陽，敏爲子景娶卓女，使卓假稱皇太弟令，拜敏揚州刺史。

translations.literal: The Wu King's attendant Gan Zhuo abandoned the palace and returned east; reaching Liyang, Min had his son Jing marry Zhuo's daughter, had Zhuo falsely proclaim an order in the name of the Grand Heir Presumptive, and appointed Min Governor of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu King's attendant Gan Zhuo left the palace and returned east. When he reached Liyang, Min had his son Jing marry Zhuo's daughter, had Zhuo issue a forged order in the name of the Grand Heir Presumptive, and appointed Min governor of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 敏使弟恢及別將錢端等南略江州，弟斌東略諸郡，江州刺史應邈、揚州刺史劉機、丹楊太守壬曠皆棄官走。

translations.literal: Min sent his younger brother Hui and detached generals such as Qian Duan south to seize Jiangzhou; his younger brother Bin east to seize the various commanderies. Jiangzhou Inspector Ying Miao, Yangzhou Inspector Liu Ji, and Danyang Administrator Ren Kuang all abandoned their posts and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Min sent his brother Hui and detached generals including Qian Duan to overrun Jiangzhou in the south, and his brother Bin to overrun commanderies in the east. Jiangzhou inspector Ying Miao, Yangzhou inspector Liu Ji, and Danyang administrator Wang Kuang all abandoned office and fled.

sentences.zh: 敏遂-{據}-有江東，以顧榮爲右將軍，賀循爲丹楊内史，周玘爲安-{豐}-太守，凡江東豪傑、名士，-{咸}-加收禮，爲將軍、郡守者四十-{餘}-人；

translations.literal: Min then held all of Jiangdong. He appointed Gu Rong Right General, He Xun Danyang Internal Secretary, and Zhou Ji Administrator of Anfeng. All the eminent men and renowned scholars of Jiangdong were recruited and honored; more than forty were made generals or commandery administrators;
translations.idiomatic: Min then controlled all of Jiangdong. He made Gu Rong Right General, He Xun internal secretary of Danyang, and Zhou Ji administrator of Anfeng. Every eminent figure and celebrated scholar in Jiangdong was recruited and honored; more than forty were appointed generals or commandery administrators;

sentences.zh: 或有老疾，就加秩命。

translations.literal: some who were old or ill were given honorary rank on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: and those who were old or infirm were given honorary titles in place.

sentences.zh: 循詐爲狂疾，得免，乃以榮領丹楊内史。

translations.literal: Xun feigned madness and was excused; Rong was then made acting Danyang Internal Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He Xun feigned madness and was excused from office; Gu Rong was then put in charge of Danyang as acting internal secretary.

sentences.zh: 玘亦稱疾，不之郡。

translations.literal: Ji also claimed illness and did not go to his commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Ji likewise pleaded illness and never took up his post.

sentences.zh: 敏疑諸名士終不爲己用，欲盡誅之。

translations.literal: Min suspected that the renowned scholars would never serve him and wanted to execute them all.
translations.idiomatic: Min suspected the eminent scholars would never truly serve him and planned to execute them all.

sentences.zh: 榮説敏曰：「中國喪亂，胡夷内侮。

translations.literal: Rong advised Min, saying, "The Central Lands are in turmoil; barbarians are invading within.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Rong urged Min, saying, "The heartland is in chaos, and barbarians are pressing in from within.

sentences.zh: 觀今日之勢，不能-{復}-振，百姓將無遺-{種}-。

translations.literal: Judging today's situation, [the dynasty] cannot revive; the common people will leave no descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Judging the situation today, the dynasty cannot be restored, and the people will be wiped out to the last man.

sentences.zh: 江南雖經石冰之亂，人物尚全，榮常憂無孫、劉之主有以存之。

translations.literal: Though Jiangnan has suffered Shi Bing's turmoil, its people are still largely intact. Rong has long worried that without a lord like Sun Quan or Liu Bei there would be no one to preserve them.
translations.idiomatic: Though Jiangnan has been ravaged by Shi Bing's rebellion, its people are still largely intact. I have long feared that without a ruler in the mold of Sun Quan or Liu Bei, there will be no one to preserve them.

sentences.zh: 今將軍神武不世，勳效已著，帶甲數萬，舳艫山積，若能委信君子，使各得盡懷，散蒂芥之嫌，塞讒諂之口，則上方數州，可傳檄而定；

translations.literal: Now, General, your divine martial prowess is unmatched in the age, your achievements are already manifest, you have tens of thousands in armor, and warships are piled like mountains. If you can entrust yourself to gentlemen of quality, let each give his full devotion, dispel petty grudges, and silence slanderers' mouths, then the several provinces above could be secured by proclamation alone;
translations.idiomatic: General, your martial prowess is unmatched in this age, your achievements are already plain, you command tens of thousands of armored men, and your warships are piled like mountains. If you place your trust in men of talent, let each give his utmost, put aside petty grievances, and shut the mouths of slanderers, then the provinces to the north could be won by proclamation alone;

sentences.zh: 不然，終不濟也。」

translations.literal: otherwise, in the end you will not succeed."
translations.idiomatic: otherwise you will never succeed in the end."

sentences.zh: 敏乃止。

translations.literal: Min then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Min then abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 敏命僚佐推己爲都督江東諸軍事、大司馬、楚公，加九錫，列上尚書，稱被中詔，自江入沔、漢，奉迎鑾駕。

translations.literal: Min ordered his staff to recommend him as Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Jiangdong, Grand Marshal, and Duke of Chu, with the Nine Bestowals. He submitted memorials to the Ministry, claiming he had received a secret edict to enter from the Yangtze into the Mian and Han rivers to escort the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Min had his staff recommend him as commander of all military affairs in Jiangdong, grand marshal, and Duke of Chu with the Nine Bestowals. He sent memorials to the Ministry of Works, claiming a secret edict had ordered him to sail from the Yangtze into the Han and Mian rivers to escort the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 太宰顒以張光爲順陽太守，帥歩騎五千詣荊州討敏。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Yong appointed Zhang Guang Shunyang Administrator and led five thousand foot and cavalry to Jingzhou to campaign against Min.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Yong appointed Zhang Guang administrator of Shunyang and led five thousand infantry and cavalry to Jingzhou to campaign against Min.

sentences.zh: 劉弘遣江夏太守陶侃、武陵太守苗光屯夏口，又遣南平太守汝南應詹督水軍以繼之。

translations.literal: Liu Hong sent Jiangxia Administrator Tao Kan and Wuling Administrator Miao Guang to encamp at Xiakou, and also sent Nanping Administrator Ying Zhan of Runan to command the navy as reinforcement.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong sent Jiangxia administrator Tao Kan and Wuling administrator Miao Guang to encamp at Xiakou, and also dispatched Nanping administrator Ying Zhan of Runan to take command of the fleet in support.

sentences.zh: 侃與敏同郡，又同歳舉吏。

translations.literal: Kan and Min were from the same commandery and had entered official service in the same year.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan and Chen Min were natives of the same commandery and had entered official service in the same year.

sentences.zh: 隨郡内史扈懷言-{於}-弘曰：「侃居大郡，統強兵，脱有異-{志}-，則荊州無東門矣！」

translations.literal: Suixian Internal Secretary Hu Huai said to Hong, "Kan holds a great commandery and commands strong troops. If he should harbor a different intent, Jingzhou would have no eastern gate!"
translations.idiomatic: Suixian internal secretary Hu Huai said to Liu Hong, "Tao Kan holds a major commandery and commands a strong force. If he should turn disloyal, Jingzhou would have lost its eastern gate!"

sentences.zh: 弘曰：「侃之忠能，吾得之已久，必無是也。」

translations.literal: Hong said, "Kan's loyalty and capability — I have known them long. There will certainly be none of that."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong replied, "I have long known Tao Kan's loyalty and ability. That will certainly not happen."

sentences.zh: 侃聞之，遣子洪及兄子臻詣弘以自固，弘引爲參軍，資而遣之。

translations.literal: When Kan heard of this, he sent his son Hong and his brother's son Zhen to Hong to affirm his loyalty. Hong took them as staff officers, provided for them, and sent them back.
translations.idiomatic: When Tao Kan heard of this, he sent his son Hong and his nephew Zhen to Liu Hong to reaffirm his loyalty. Hong took them on as staff officers, provided for them, and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 曰：「賢叔-{征}-行，君祖母年髙，便可歸也。

translations.literal: He said, "Your worthy uncle is on campaign; your grandmother is advanced in years — you may return home.
translations.idiomatic: He told them, "Your worthy uncle is on campaign, and your grandmother is very old. You should go home.

sentences.zh: 匹夫之交，尚不負心，況大丈夫乎！」

translations.literal: The friendship of common men does not even betray the heart — how much more so a great man!"
translations.idiomatic: Even the friendship of common men does not betray the heart — how much less should a great man do so!"

sentences.zh: 敏以陳恢爲荊州刺史，寇武昌；

translations.literal: Min appointed Chen Hui Governor of Jingzhou and raided Wuchang;
translations.idiomatic: Min made Chen Hui governor of Jingzhou and raided Wuchang;

sentences.zh: 弘加侃前鋒督護以-{御}-之。

translations.literal: Hong gave Kan the additional title Vanguard Supervisor to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong gave Tao Kan the additional title of vanguard supervisor to resist him.

sentences.zh: 侃以運船爲戰艦，或以爲不可。

translations.literal: Kan used transport ships as warships; some thought this unwise.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan converted transport vessels into warships, and some considered that imprudent.

sentences.zh: 侃曰：「用官船撃官賊，何爲不可！」

translations.literal: Kan said, "Using government ships to attack government rebels — why would that be wrong!"
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan said, "Using government ships to strike government rebels — what could be wrong with that!"

sentences.zh: 侃與恢戰，屢破之；

translations.literal: Kan fought Hui and repeatedly defeated him;
translations.idiomatic: He fought Chen Hui again and again and routed him each time;

sentences.zh: 又與皮初、張光、苗光共破錢端-{於}-長岐。

translations.literal: he also joined Pi Chu, Zhang Guang, and Miao Guang in defeating Qian Duan at Changqi.
translations.idiomatic: and together with Pi Chu, Zhang Guang, and Miao Guang he defeated Qian Duan at Changqi.

sentences.zh: 南陽太守衞展説弘曰：「張光，太宰腹心，公旣與東海，宜斬光以明向背。」

translations.literal: Nanyang Administrator Wei Zhan advised Hong, saying, "Zhang Guang is the Grand Preceptor's trusted man. Since you have allied with Donghai, you should execute Guang to show which side you are on."
translations.idiomatic: Nanyang administrator Wei Zhan urged Liu Hong, "Zhang Guang is the Grand Preceptor's trusted man. Since you have sided with Donghai, you ought to execute Guang to make your allegiance plain."

sentences.zh: 弘曰：「宰輔得失，豈張光之罪！

translations.literal: Hong said, "The chancellor's success or failure — how is that Zhang Guang's crime!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong replied, "Whether the chief minister succeeds or fails — how is that Zhang Guang's fault!

sentences.zh: 危人自安，君子弗爲也。」

translations.literal: Endangering others to secure oneself — a gentleman does not do that."
translations.idiomatic: Endangering others to save oneself is something a gentleman does not do."

sentences.zh: 乃表光殊勳，乞加遷擢。

translations.literal: He then memorialized Guang's exceptional merit and requested promotion for him.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized Zhang Guang's outstanding service and asked that he be promoted.

sentences.zh: 是歳，離石大饑，漢王淵徙屯黎亭，就邸閣-{谷}-；

translations.literal: That year Lishi suffered great famine. Han King Yuan moved his camp to Liting to draw on the government granary;
translations.idiomatic: That year Lishi suffered a severe famine. Han King Liu Yuan moved his camp to Liting to draw grain from the government storehouse;

sentences.zh: 留太尉宏守離石，使大司農-{卜}-豫運糧以給之。

translations.literal: he left Grand Commandant Hong to guard Lishi and sent Grand Minister of Agriculture Bu Yu to transport grain to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: he left Grand Commandant Liu Hong to hold Lishi and sent Grand Minister of Agriculture Bu Yu to transport grain for their relief.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，戊子朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on the first day of the month (day wuzi), there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the new moon of day wuzi, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 初，太弟中庶子蘭陵繆播有寵-{於}-司空越；

translations.literal: Earlier, the Heir Presumptive's Central Palace Attendant Miu Bo of Lanling had the favor of Minister over the Masses Yue;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Heir Presumptive's central palace attendant Miu Bo of Lanling had won the favor of Minister over the Masses Yue;

sentences.zh: 播從弟右衞率胤，太宰顒前妃之弟也。

translations.literal: Bo's younger cousin by the maternal line, Right Defender of the Heir Yin, was the former Grand Preceptor Yong's consort's brother.
translations.idiomatic: Bo's younger cousin Yin, right defender of the Heir, was a brother of Grand Preceptor Yong's former consort.

sentences.zh: 越之起兵，遣播、胤詣長安説顒，令奉帝還洛，約與顒分陝爲伯。

translations.literal: When Yue raised his army, he sent Bo and Yin to Chang'an to persuade Yong to escort the Emperor back to Luoyang, agreeing with Yong to divide at Shan and each become a marquis.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue raised his army, he sent Bo and Yin to Chang'an to persuade Yong to escort the emperor back to Luoyang, proposing that they divide the realm at Shan Pass and each rule as a feudal lord.

sentences.zh: 顒素信重播兄弟，卽欲從之。

translations.literal: Yong had always trusted and valued the Bo brothers and immediately wanted to agree.
translations.idiomatic: Yong had long trusted and esteemed the Bo brothers and was ready to accept at once.

sentences.zh: 張方自以罪重，恐爲誅首，謂顒曰：「今-{據}-形勝之地，國富兵強，奉天子以號令，誰敢不從，奈何拱手受-{制}--{於}-人！」

translations.literal: Zhang Fang, considering his crimes grave and fearing to be the first executed, said to Yong, "Now we hold strategically superior ground; the state is rich and troops are strong. Obey the Son of Heaven and issue commands — who would dare disobey? Why submit passively to others' control!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fang, knowing his crimes were grave and fearing he would be the first man executed, said to Yong, "We now hold commanding ground, the state is rich and our armies are strong. Upheld by the Son of Heaven, we can issue orders at will — who would dare disobey? Why surrender passively to others!"

sentences.zh: 顒乃止。

translations.literal: Yong then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Yong then abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 及劉喬敗，顒懼，欲罷兵，與山東和解。

translations.literal: When Liu Qiao was defeated, Yong grew afraid and wished to cease hostilities and reconcile with the eastern provinces.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Qiao was defeated, Yong grew fearful and wished to cease fighting and make peace with the eastern provinces.

sentences.zh: 恐張方不從，猶豫未決。

translations.literal: Fearing Zhang Fang would not comply, he hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Zhang Fang would refuse, he wavered and could not decide.

sentences.zh: 方素與長安富人郅輔親善，以爲帳下督。

translations.literal: Fang had long been on close terms with the Chang'an magnate Zhi Fu and made him his camp supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Fang had long been intimate with the wealthy Chang'an man Zhi Fu and appointed him supervisor of his camp.

sentences.zh: 顒參軍河間畢垣，嘗爲方所侮，因説顒曰：「張方久屯霸上，聞山東兵盛，盤桓不進，宜防其未萌。

translations.literal: Yong's staff officer Bi Yuan of Hejian, once humiliated by Fang, therefore advised Yong, saying, "Zhang Fang has long encamped at Bashang. Hearing that eastern troops are strong, he lingers without advancing — guard against trouble before it sprouts.
translations.idiomatic: Yong's staff officer Bi Yuan of Hejian, whom Fang had once insulted, therefore urged Yong, "Zhang Fang has long been encamped at Bashang. Hearing that the eastern armies are strong, he hangs back and will not advance. You should guard against trouble before it takes root.

sentences.zh: 其親信郅輔縣具其謀。」

translations.literal: His trusted man Zhi Fu knows his plot in full detail."
translations.idiomatic: His confidant Zhi Fu knows the whole of his scheme."

sentences.zh: 繆播、繆胤-{復}-説顒：「宜急斬方以謝，山東可不勞而定。」

translations.literal: Miu Bo and Miu Yin again advised Yong, "You should urgently execute Fang to make amends; the east could be settled without effort."
translations.idiomatic: Miu Bo and Miu Yin again urged Yong, "You should execute Fang at once to make amends. The east could then be pacified without a fight."

sentences.zh: 顒使人召輔，垣迎説輔曰：「張方欲反，人謂卿知之。

translations.literal: Yong sent someone to summon Fu. Yuan met Fu and said, "Zhang Fang intends to rebel; people say you know of it.
translations.idiomatic: Yong sent for Fu. Bi Yuan intercepted him and said, "Zhang Fang is plotting rebellion, and people say you know about it.

sentences.zh: 王若問卿，何辭以對？」

translations.literal: If the Prince asks you, what words will you use to answer?"
translations.idiomatic: If the prince questions you, what will you say?"

sentences.zh: 輔驚曰：「實不聞方反，爲之奈何？」

translations.literal: Fu said in alarm, "I truly have not heard that Fang is rebelling — what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Fu said in alarm, "I truly have not heard that Fang is rebelling. What am I to do?"

sentences.zh: 垣曰：「王若問卿，但言爾爾；

translations.literal: Yuan said, "If the Prince asks you, just say 'indeed, indeed';
translations.idiomatic: Bi Yuan said, "If the prince asks you, simply say, 'Indeed, indeed';

sentences.zh: 不然，必不免禍。」

translations.literal: otherwise you will surely not escape disaster."
translations.idiomatic: otherwise you will surely not escape disaster."

sentences.zh: 輔入，顒問之曰：「張方反，卿知之乎？」

translations.literal: Fu entered. Yong asked him, "Zhang Fang is rebelling — do you know of it?"
translations.idiomatic: Fu went in. Yong asked him, "Zhang Fang is rebelling. Do you know of it?"

sentences.zh: 輔曰：「爾。」

translations.literal: Fu said, "Indeed."
translations.idiomatic: Fu said, "Indeed."

sentences.zh: 顒曰：「遣卿取之，可乎？」

translations.literal: Yong said, "Send you to take him — acceptable?"
translations.idiomatic: Yong said, "If I send you to take him, will that do?"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「爾。」

translations.literal: He again said, "Indeed."
translations.idiomatic: Fu again said, "Indeed."

sentences.zh: 顒-{於}-是使輔送書-{於}-方，因殺之。

translations.literal: Yong then sent Fu to deliver a letter to Fang and thereby kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Yong then sent Fu to deliver a letter to Fang and kill him in the act.

sentences.zh: 輔旣暱-{於}-方，持刀而入，守閣者不疑。

translations.literal: Fu being intimate with Fang, he entered with a blade in hand; the gate guards suspected nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Because Fu was close to Fang, he entered carrying a sword, and the gate guards suspected nothing.

sentences.zh: 方火下-{發}-函，輔斬其頭。

translations.literal: Fang, by lamplight, was opening the letter when Fu cut off his head.
translations.idiomatic: Fang was by lamplight breaking the seal on the letter when Fu struck off his head.

sentences.zh: 還報，顒以輔爲安定太守。

translations.literal: Returning to report, Yong appointed Fu Administrator of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to report, Yong appointed Fu administrator of Anding.

sentences.zh: 送方頭-{於}-司空越以請和；

translations.literal: He sent Fang's head to Minister over the Masses Yue to sue for peace;
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zhang Fang's head to Minister over the Masses Yue to sue for peace;

sentences.zh: 越不許。

translations.literal: Yue did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Yue refused.

sentences.zh: 宋冑襲河橋，樓褒西走。

translations.literal: Song Zhou attacked the Yellow River bridge; Lou Bao fled west.
translations.idiomatic: Song Zhou attacked the Yellow River bridge, and Lou Bao fled west.

sentences.zh: 平昌公模遣前鋒督護馮-{嵩}-會宋冑逼洛陽。

translations.literal: Prince of Pingchang Mo sent Vanguard Supervisor Feng Song to join Song Zhou and press on Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Pingchang Mo sent vanguard supervisor Feng Song to join Song Zhou and press toward Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 成都王穎西奔長安，至華陰，聞顒已與山東和親，留不敢進。

translations.literal: Prince of Chengdu Ying fled west to Chang'an. Reaching Huayin, he heard Yong had reconciled with the eastern provinces and halted, not daring to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Chengdu Ying fled west toward Chang'an. When he reached Huayin and heard that Yong had made peace with the eastern provinces, he halted and dared not go on.

sentences.zh: 呂朗屯滎陽，劉琨以張方首示之，遂降。

translations.literal: Lu Lang was encamped at Xingyang. Liu Kun showed him Zhang Fang's head, and he surrendered at once.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Lang was encamped at Xingyang. Liu Kun displayed Zhang Fang's head to him, and he surrendered at once.

sentences.zh: 甲子，司空越遣祁弘、宋冑、司馬纂帥鮮卑西迎車駕，以周馥爲司隸校尉、假節，都督諸軍，屯澠池。

translations.literal: On day jiazi, Minister over the Masses Yue sent Qi Hong, Song Zhou, and Sima Zuan leading Xianbei west to welcome the imperial carriage. He appointed Zhou Fu Metropolitan Commandant with credentials, supervising all armies, encamped at Mianchi.
translations.idiomatic: On day jiazi, Minister over the Masses Yue sent Qi Hong, Song Zhou, and Sima Zuan at the head of Xianbei forces west to welcome the imperial carriage. He made Zhou Fu metropolitan commandant with credentials to supervise all armies and encamped him at Mianchi.

sentences.zh: 三月，惤令劉柏根反，衆以萬數，自稱惤公。

translations.literal: Third month: the Evil-Exorcising Magistrate Liu Bogen rebelled; followers numbered in the tens of thousands; he styled himself Duke of Evil-Exorcism.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, the evil-exorcising magistrate Liu Bogen rebelled. His followers numbered in the tens of thousands, and he styled himself Duke of Exorcism.

sentences.zh: 王彌帥家僮從之，柏根以彌爲長史，彌從父弟桑爲東中郎將。

translations.literal: Wang Mi led household retainers to join him. Bogen made Mi his Chief Clerk; Mi's cousin Sang became Eastern Central Cadet-General.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mi led his household retainers to join him. Bogen made Mi his chief clerk and Mi's cousin Sang eastern central cadet-general.

sentences.zh: 柏根寇臨淄，靑州都督髙密王略使劉暾將兵拒之；

translations.literal: Bogen raided Linzi. Qingzhou Commander-in-Chief Prince of Gaomi Lue sent Liu Dun with troops to resist;
translations.idiomatic: Bogen raided Linzi. Qingzhou commander-in-chief Prince of Gaomi Wang Lue sent Liu Dun with troops to resist him;

sentences.zh: 暾兵敗，奔洛陽，略走保聊城。

translations.literal: Dun's army was defeated; he fled to Luoyang. Lue fled to hold Liaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Dun was defeated and fled to Luoyang. Wang Lue withdrew to defend Liaocheng.

sentences.zh: 王浚遣將討柏根，斬之。

translations.literal: Wang Jun sent a general to campaign against Bogen and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun sent a general against Bogen and had him beheaded.

sentences.zh: 王彌亡入長廣山爲群盜。

translations.literal: Wang Mi fled into Mount Changguang and became a bandit chief.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mi fled into Mount Changguang and became leader of a band of robbers.

sentences.zh: -{寧}-州頻歳饑疫，死者以十萬計。

translations.literal: Ning province year after year suffered famine and pestilence; the dead numbered in the hundreds of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Ning province suffered famine and plague year after year; the dead were reckoned in the hundreds of thousands.

sentences.zh: 五苓夷強盛，州兵屢敗。

translations.literal: The Wulingyi grew powerful; provincial troops were repeatedly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The Wulingyi grew powerful, and the provincial army was repeatedly defeated.

sentences.zh: 吏民流入交州者甚衆，夷遂圍州城。

translations.literal: Officials and commoners fleeing into Jiaozhou were very numerous; the barbarians then besieged the provincial capital.
translations.idiomatic: Great numbers of officials and commoners fled into Jiaozhou, and the barbarians then besieged the provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 李毅疾病，救援路絶，乃上疎言：「不能式遏寇虐，坐待殄斃。

translations.literal: Li Yi was ill; relief routes were cut off. He submitted a memorial saying, "Unable to restrain the invaders' cruelty, I sit awaiting annihilation.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yi fell ill, and the routes of relief were cut off. He submitted a memorial saying, "I am unable to check the invaders' cruelty and can only sit awaiting destruction.

sentences.zh: 若不垂矜恤，乞降大使，及臣尚存，加臣重-{辟}-；

translations.literal: If Your Majesty will not show compassionate regard, I beg you send a great envoy; while I yet live, impose upon me heavy punishment;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty will not show compassionate regard, I beg that a high envoy be sent. While I yet live, impose the heaviest punishment upon me;

sentences.zh: 若臣已死，陳屍爲戮。」

translations.literal: if I am already dead, display my corpse for execution."
translations.idiomatic: if I am already dead, let my corpse be displayed for punishment."

sentences.zh: 朝廷不報，積數年，子釗自洛往省之，未至，毅卒。

translations.literal: The court gave no reply. After several years, his son Zhao went from Luoyang to visit him but had not arrived when Yi died.
translations.idiomatic: The court gave no reply. After several years his son Zhao set out from Luoyang to visit him, but had not arrived when Yi died.

sentences.zh: 毅女秀，明達有父風，衆推秀領-{寧}-州事。

translations.literal: Yi's daughter Xiu was clear-sighted and bore her father's manner; the multitude pushed Xiu to take charge of Ning province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's daughter Xiu was clear-sighted and had her father's bearing; the people urged Xiu to take charge of Ning province.

sentences.zh: 秀獎厲戰士，嬰城固守。

translations.literal: Xiu encouraged and roused the warriors, tied the city, and held firm.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu encouraged the fighting men and held the city under siege.

sentences.zh: 城中糧盡，炙鼠拔草而食之。

translations.literal: When grain in the city was exhausted, they roasted rats and pulled up grass to eat.
translations.idiomatic: When food in the city ran out, they roasted rats and pulled up grass to eat.

sentences.zh: 伺夷稍怠，輒出兵掩撃，破之。

translations.literal: Watching for the barbarians' slackening, she would sortie troops in surprise attacks and defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever she saw the barbarians relax their guard, she sent troops out in surprise attacks and routed them.

sentences.zh: -{范}-長生詣成都，成都王雄門迎，執版，拜爲丞相，尊之曰-{范}-賢。

translations.literal: Fan Changsheng went to Chengdu. Prince of Chengdu Xiong met him at the gate, presented the tablet, appointed him Chancellor, and honored him as Lord Fan the Worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Changsheng went to Chengdu. Prince of Chengdu Li Xiong met him at the gate, presented the investiture tablet, appointed him chancellor, and honored him as Lord Fan the Worthy.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，己巳，司空越引兵屯温。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, on day jisi, Minister over the Masses Yue led troops to encamp at Wen.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on day jisi, Minister over the Masses Yue led his army to encamp at Wen.

sentences.zh: 初，太宰顒以爲張方死，東方兵必可解。

translations.literal: At first, Grand Preceptor Yong thought that with Zhang Fang dead, the eastern armies would surely be dissolved.
translations.idiomatic: At first Grand Preceptor Yong believed that once Zhang Fang was dead, the eastern armies would surely disband.

sentences.zh: 旣而東方兵聞方死，爭入關，顒悔之，乃斬郅輔，遣弘農太守彭隨、北地太守刁默將兵拒祁弘等-{於}-湖。

translations.literal: But then when the eastern armies heard Fang was dead, they vied to enter the passes. Yong regretted it; he then executed Zhi Fu and sent Administrator of Hongnong Peng Sui and Administrator of Beidi Diao Mo with troops to resist Qi Hong and others at Hu.
translations.idiomatic: But when the eastern armies heard that Fang was dead, they rushed to enter the passes. Yong regretted his decision, executed Zhi Fu, and sent Peng Sui, administrator of Hongnong, and Diao Mo, administrator of Beidi, with troops to block Qi Hong and the others at Hu.

sentences.zh: 五月，壬辰，弘等撃隨、默，大破之。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day renchen, Hong and others attacked Sui and Mo and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on day renchen, Hong and his forces attacked Sui and Mo and routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 遂西入關，又敗顒將馬瞻、郭偉-{於}-霸水，顒單馬逃入太白山。

translations.literal: They then entered the passes westward, again defeated Yong's generals Ma Zhan and Guo Wei at Bashui; Yong fled alone on horseback into Taibai Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: They then pushed west into the passes and again defeated Yong's generals Ma Zhan and Guo Wei at Bashui. Yong fled alone on horseback into the Taibai Mountains.

sentences.zh: 弘等入長安，所部鮮卑大掠，殺二萬-{餘}-人，百官奔散，入山中，拾橡實食之。

translations.literal: Hong and others entered Chang'an; the Xianbei under their command plundered extensively, killing more than twenty thousand; the hundred officials fled in all directions, went into the mountains, and gathered acorns to eat.
translations.idiomatic: Hong and his men entered Chang'an. The Xianbei in their ranks looted on a vast scale and killed more than twenty thousand people. Officials fled in every direction into the hills, gathering acorns to survive.

sentences.zh: 己亥，弘等奉帝乘牛車東還。

translations.literal: Day jihai, Hong and others escorted the Emperor east on an ox cart.
translations.idiomatic: On day jihai, Hong and his followers escorted the emperor eastward in an ox cart.

sentences.zh: 以太弟太保梁柳爲鎭西將軍，守關中。

translations.literal: They appointed the Heir Presumptive's Grand Mentor Liang Liu as General Who Pacifies the West to guard Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: They appointed Liang Liu, grand mentor to the heir presumptive, as General Who Pacifies the West to hold Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 六月，丙辰朔，帝至洛陽，-{復}-羊-{後}-。

translations.literal: Sixth month, new moon of day bingchen, the Emperor arrived at Luoyang and restored Empress Yang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the new moon of day bingchen, the emperor reached Luoyang and restored Empress Yang.

sentences.zh: 辛未，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: Day xinwei, general amnesty; era name changed.
translations.idiomatic: On day xinwei there was a general amnesty and the era name was changed.

sentences.zh: 馬瞻等入長安，殺梁柳，與始平太守梁邁共迎太宰顒-{於}-南山。

translations.literal: Ma Zhan and others entered Chang'an, killed Liang Liu, and together with Administrator of Shiping Liang Mai welcomed Grand Preceptor Yong from South Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zhan and his men entered Chang'an, killed Liang Liu, and together with Liang Mai, administrator of Shiping, went to South Mountain to welcome Grand Preceptor Yong back.

sentences.zh: 弘農太守裴廙、秦國内史賈龕、安定太守賈疋等起兵撃顒，斬馬瞻、梁邁。

translations.literal: Administrator of Hongnong Pei Guang, Interior Minister of Qin Jia Kan, Administrator of Anding Jia Pi, and others raised armies to attack Yong and executed Ma Zhan and Liang Mai.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Guang, administrator of Hongnong, Jia Kan, interior minister of Qin, Jia Pi, administrator of Anding, and others raised forces against Yong and beheaded Ma Zhan and Liang Mai.

sentences.zh: 疋，詡之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Pi was the great-grandson of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Pi was the great-grandson of Jia Xu.

sentences.zh: 司空越遣督護麋晃將兵撃顒，至鄭，顒使平北將軍牽秀屯馮翊。

translations.literal: Minister over the Masses Yue sent Supervising Protector Mi Huang with troops to attack Yong; reaching Zheng, Yong sent General Who Pacifies the North Qian Xiu to encamp at Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Minister over the Masses Yue dispatched Supervising Protector Mi Huang with an army against Yong. When Huang reached Zheng, Yong sent General Who Pacifies the North Qian Xiu to hold Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 顒長史楊騰，詐稱顒命，使秀罷兵，騰遂殺秀，關中皆服-{於}-越，顒保城而已。

translations.literal: Yong's Chief Clerk Yang Teng falsely claimed Yong's order to make Xiu cease fighting; Teng then killed Xiu; all Guanzhong submitted to Yue; Yong merely held the city.
translations.idiomatic: Yong's chief clerk Yang Teng forged an order in Yong's name telling Xiu to stand down, then killed Xiu. All of Guanzhong submitted to Yue, and Yong was reduced to defending the city alone.

sentences.zh: 成都王雄卽皇帝位，大赦，改元曰晏平，國號大成。

translations.literal: Prince of Chengdu Xiong assumed the emperor's throne, general amnesty; changed era name to Yanping; state name Dacheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Chengdu, Li Xiong, took the imperial throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, changed the era name to Yanping, and named his state Dacheng.

sentences.zh: 追尊父特曰景皇帝，廟號始祖；

translations.literal: Posthumously honored father Te as Emperor Jing, temple name Shizu;
translations.idiomatic: He posthumously honored his father Li Te as Emperor Jing, with the temple name Founding Ancestor;

sentences.zh: 尊王太-{后}-曰皇太-{后}-。

translations.literal: Honored the Queen Mother as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: and elevated the queen mother to empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 以-{范}-長生爲天地太師；

translations.literal: Appointed Fan Changsheng as Grand Master of Heaven and Earth;
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Fan Changsheng Grand Master of Heaven and Earth;

translations.literal: Restored his retainers; all were exempt from taxes and levies.
translations.idiomatic: restored his followers to their ranks, and exempted them all from taxes and corvée.

sentences.zh: 諸將恃恩，互爭班位，尚書令閻式上疎，請考漢、晉故事，立百官-{制}-度，從之。

translations.literal: The generals relied on favor and vied with one another for rank and position; Supervisor of the Masters of Writing Yan Shi submitted a memorial requesting examination of Han and Jin precedents to establish regulations for the hundred officials; this was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The generals, trusting in royal favor, fought over precedence. Supervisor of the Masters of Writing Yan Shi submitted a memorial asking that Han and Jin precedents be studied to set up a formal bureaucracy, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，乙酉朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, new moon of day yiyou; there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on the new moon of day yiyou, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 八月，以司空越爲太傅，録尚書事；

translations.literal: Eighth month, Minister over the Masses Yue was made Grand Tutor and recorded matters of the Masters of Writing;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Minister over the Masses Yue was appointed Grand Tutor with authority to record matters of the Masters of Writing;

sentences.zh: -{范}-陽王虓爲司空，鎭鄴；

translations.literal: Prince of Fanyang Chou was made Minister over the Masses and stationed at Ye;
translations.idiomatic: the Prince of Fanyang, Sima Chou, became Minister over the Masses and took up station at Ye;

sentences.zh: 平昌公模爲鎭東大將軍，鎭許昌；

translations.literal: Duke of Pingchang Mo was made General Who Pacifies the East and stationed at Xuchang;
translations.idiomatic: the Duke of Pingchang, Sima Mo, became General Who Pacifies the East and held Xuchang;

sentences.zh: 王浚爲驃騎大將軍、都督東夷、河北諸軍事，領幽州刺史。

translations.literal: Wang Jun was made Grand General of Agile Cavalry, overseer of military affairs of the Eastern Yi and Hebei, and held the governorship of You Province.
translations.idiomatic: and Wang Jun was made Grand General of Agile Cavalry, commander of armies in the east and on the Hebei frontier, with concurrent appointment as governor of You Province.

sentences.zh: 越以吏部郎穎川庚敳爲軍諮祭酒，前太弟中庶子胡母輔之爲從事中郎，黃門侍郎河南郭象爲主簿，鴻臚丞阮修爲行參軍，謝鯤爲掾。

translations.literal: Yue appointed Lang of the Ministry of Personnel Geng Kai of Yingchuan as Army Advisory Libationer; former Central Palace Attendant of the Heir Presumptive Humu Fuzhi as Attendant Gentleman; Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates Guo Xiang of Henan as Chief Clerk; Vice Director of the Imperial Stud Ruan Xiu as Acting Army Assistant; and Xie Kun as adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: Yue named Geng Kai of Yingchuan, a lang in the Ministry of Personnel, army advisory libationer; Humu Fuzhi, former central palace attendant to the heir presumptive, attendant gentleman; Guo Xiang of Henan, gentleman at the yellow gates, chief clerk; Ruan Xiu, vice director of the imperial stud, acting army assistant; and Xie Kun as staff adjutant.

sentences.zh: 輔之-{薦}-樂安光逸-{於}-越，越亦-{辟}-之。

translations.literal: Fuzhi recommended Guang Yi of Le'an to Yue, and Yue also recruited him.
translations.idiomatic: Fuzhi recommended Guang Yi of Le'an to Yue, and Yue recruited him as well.

sentences.zh: 敳等皆尚虚玄，不以世務嬰心，縱酒放誕；

translations.literal: Kai and the others all prized voidness and profundity, did not burden their hearts with worldly affairs, and indulged in drink and unrestrained conduct;
translations.idiomatic: Kai and his circle all cultivated abstruse philosophy, shrugged off public business, and gave themselves to wine and wild behavior;

sentences.zh: 敳殖貨無厭；

translations.literal: Kai amassed goods without satiety;
translations.idiomatic: Kai hoarded wealth without limit;

sentences.zh: 象薄行，好招權；

translations.literal: Xiang had slight conduct and loved to gather power;
translations.idiomatic: Xiang's morals were thin and he loved to grasp power;

sentences.zh: 越皆以其名重-{於}-世，故-{辟}-之。

translations.literal: Yue recruited them all because their renown was weighty in the world.
translations.idiomatic: yet Yue brought them all in because their names carried weight across the realm.

sentences.zh: 祁弘之入關也，成都王穎自武關奔新野。

translations.literal: When Qi Hong entered the passes, Prince of Chengdu Ying fled from Wuguan to Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi Hong marched into the passes, the Prince of Chengdu, Sima Ying, fled from Wuguan to Xinye.

sentences.zh: 會新城元公劉弘卒，司馬郭勱作亂，欲迎穎爲主，治中順陽；

translations.literal: When Duke Yuan of Xincheng Liu Hong died, Marshal Guo Xun rebelled and wished to welcome Ying as ruler; Administrator of Shunyang;
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Hong, Duke Yuan of Xincheng, died, his marshal Guo Xun rose in revolt and tried to install Ying as lord; the administrator of Shunyang

sentences.zh: 郭舒奉弘子璠以討勱，斬之。

translations.literal: Guo Shu supported Hong's son Fan to attack Xun and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Shu rallied Hong's son Liu Fan to suppress Xun and cut off his head.

sentences.zh: 詔南中郎將劉陶收穎。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Central Leader of the South Liu Tao to capture Ying.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Central Leader of the South Liu Tao to take Ying into custody.

sentences.zh: 穎北渡河，奔朝歌，收故將士，得數百人，欲赴公師籓。

translations.literal: Ying crossed the river north, fled to Chaoge, gathered former officers and soldiers, obtained several hundred men, and wished to join Gongshi Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Ying crossed the Yellow River northward, fled to Chaoge, rallied a few hundred of his old officers and men, and planned to join Gongshi Fan.

sentences.zh: 九月，頓丘太守馮-{嵩}-執之，送鄴；

translations.literal: Ninth month, Administrator of Dunqiu Feng Song apprehended him and sent him to Ye;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Feng Song, administrator of Dunqiu, seized him and sent him to Ye;

sentences.zh: -{范}-陽王虓不忍殺而幽之。

translations.literal: Prince of Fanyang Chou could not bear to kill him and imprisoned him instead.
translations.idiomatic: the Prince of Fanyang, Sima Chou, could not bring himself to execute Ying and kept him under house arrest instead.

sentences.zh: 公師籓自白馬南渡河，兗州刺史苟晞討斬之。

translations.literal: Gongshi Fan crossed the river south from Baima; Governor of Yan Province Gou Xi attacked and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Gongshi Fan crossed south from Baima, but Gou Xi, governor of Yan Province, pursued him and cut off his head.

sentences.zh: 進東贏公騰爵爲東燕王，平昌公模爲南陽王。

translations.literal: Duke of Dongying Teng was advanced in rank to Prince of Dongyan; Duke of Pingchang Mo to Prince of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Teng of Dongying was raised to Prince of Dongyan, and Duke Mo of Pingchang to Prince of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，-{范}-陽王虓薨。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, Prince of Fanyang Chou died.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, the Prince of Fanyang, Sima Chou, died.

sentences.zh: 長史劉輿以成都王穎素爲鄴人所附，秘不-{發}-喪，偽令人爲-{臺}-使稱詔，夜，賜穎死，-{並}-殺其二子。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Liu Yu, because Prince of Chengdu Ying had always been favored by the people of Ye, kept the death secret, had someone falsely pose as an envoy from the court bearing an edict, and in the night ordered Ying to die, also killing his two sons.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Liu Yu, knowing that the people of Ye had long favored the Prince of Chengdu, concealed Chou's death. He sent a man disguised as an imperial messenger with a forged edict and, that night, had Ying put to death along with his two sons.

sentences.zh: 穎官屬先皆逃散，惟盧-{志}-隨從，至死不怠，收而殯之。

translations.literal: Ying's officials had all fled; only Lu Zhi followed to the end without slackening, gathered the body, and buried it.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's staff had already scattered; only Lu Zhi stayed with him to the end, then gathered his body and gave him burial.

sentences.zh: 太傅越召-{志}-爲軍諮祭酒。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Yue summoned Zhi as Army Advisory Libationer.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Yue then summoned Lu Zhi and made him army advisory libationer.

sentences.zh: 越將召劉輿，或曰：「輿猶膩也，近則汚人。」

translations.literal: Yue was about to summon Liu Yu; someone said, "Yu is like grease — if you draw near, he soils you."
translations.idiomatic: Yue was on the point of calling Liu Yu into service when someone warned him, "Yu is like grease — get close and he stains you."

sentences.zh: 及至，越疎之。

translations.literal: When he arrived, Yue kept him at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu arrived, Yue kept him at arm's length.

sentences.zh: 輿密視天下兵簿及倉庫、牛馬、器械、水陸之形，皆默識之。

translations.literal: Yu secretly examined the empire's military registers, warehouses, cattle and horses, weapons, and land and water terrain, memorizing all of them.
translations.idiomatic: Yu quietly studied the empire's troop rolls, storehouses, livestock, arms, and the lay of land and water, committing every detail to memory.

sentences.zh: 時軍國多事，毎會議，自長史潘滔以下，莫知所對；

translations.literal: At that time state and army affairs were many; at every conference, from Chief Clerk Pan Tao downward, none knew how to respond;
translations.idiomatic: With war and government in constant crisis, every council meeting left Chief Clerk Pan Tao and the rest speechless;

sentences.zh: 輿應機辨畫，越傾膝酬接，卽以爲左長史，軍國之務，悉以委之。

translations.literal: Yu responded opportunely with plans and arguments; Yue bent his knee in engagement and immediately made him Left Chief Clerk, entrusting all military and state affairs to him.
translations.idiomatic: but Yu answered on the spot with sharp plans. Yue leaned in to hear him and at once appointed him left chief clerk, handing him the whole weight of civil and military affairs.

sentences.zh: 輿説越遣其弟琨鎭并州，以爲北-{面}-之重；

translations.literal: Yu persuaded Yue to send his younger brother Kun to govern Bing Province as the weight of the northern frontier;
translations.idiomatic: Yu urged Yue to post his younger brother Kun in Bing Province as the anchor of the northern frontier;

sentences.zh: 越表琨爲并州刺史，以東燕王騰爲車騎將軍、都督鄴城諸軍事，鎭鄴。

translations.literal: Yue memorialized Kun as Governor of Bing Province and made Prince of Dongyan Teng General of Chariots and Cavalry, overseer of military affairs at Ye, stationed at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Yue recommended Kun for governor of Bing and made Prince Teng of Dongyan general of chariots and cavalry with command at Ye, where Teng took up residence.

sentences.zh: 十一月，己巳，夜，帝食餅中毒，庚午，崩-{於}-顯陽殿。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, day jisi, at night the Emperor was poisoned eating cakes; day gengwu, he died in the Xianyang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on day jisi, the emperor was poisoned by cakes in the night; on day gengwu he died in the Xianyang Hall.

sentences.zh: 羊-{後}-自以-{於}-太弟熾爲嫂，恐不得爲太-{后}-，將立淸河王覃。
