translations.literal: Empress Yang, considering herself sister-in-law to the Heir Presumptive Chi, feared she could not become Empress Dowager and intended to install Prince of Qinghe Tan.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yang, viewing herself as sister-in-law to the heir presumptive Sima Chi, feared she would never be made empress dowager and plotted to enthrone the Prince of Qinghe, Sima Tan.

sentences.zh: 侍中華混諫曰：「太弟在東宮已久，民望素定，今日-{寧}-可易乎！」

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary Hua Hun remonstrated, "The Heir Presumptive has been in the Eastern Palace long; popular expectation is already settled — how can we change today!"
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-Ordinary Hua Hun remonstrated, "The heir presumptive has sat in the Eastern Palace for years and the people's hopes are fixed — how can we change course now!"

sentences.zh: 卽露版馳告太傅越，召太弟入宮。

translations.literal: He immediately sent an open letter in haste to report to Grand Tutor Yue and summoned the Heir Presumptive into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He at once sent an open dispatch racing to Grand Tutor Yue and called the heir presumptive into the palace.

sentences.zh: -{後}-已召覃至尚書閣，疑變，-{托}-疾而返。

translations.literal: The Empress had already summoned Tan to the Masters of Writing pavilion; suspecting a change, she pleaded illness and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The empress had already summoned Tan to the Masters of Writing offices; sensing a shift, she feigned illness and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，太弟卽皇帝位，大赦，尊皇-{后}-曰惠皇-{后}-，居弘訓宮；

translations.literal: Day guiyou, the Heir Presumptive assumed the emperor's throne, general amnesty; honored the Empress as Empress Hui, dwelling in the Hongxun Palace;
translations.idiomatic: On day guiyou the heir presumptive took the throne and proclaimed a general amnesty. He honored the former empress as Empress Hui and installed her in the Hongxun Palace;

sentences.zh: 追尊母王-{才}-人曰皇太-{后}-；

translations.literal: Posthumously honored his mother Lady Wang as Empress Dowager;
translations.idiomatic: posthumously raised his mother, Lady Wang, to empress dowager;

sentences.zh: 立妃梁氏爲皇-{后}-。

translations.literal: Installed consort Lady Liang as Empress.
translations.idiomatic: and made his consort, Lady Liang, empress.

sentences.zh: 懷帝始遵舊-{制}-，-{於}-東堂-{聽}-政。

translations.literal: Emperor Huai began to follow the old regulations, holding court at the Eastern Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huai began to follow the old custom of hearing affairs at the Eastern Hall.

sentences.zh: 毎至宴會，輒與群官論衆務，考經籍。

translations.literal: At every feast he would discuss many affairs with the assembled officials and examine the classics.
translations.idiomatic: At every banquet he debated state business with his officials and tested them against the classics.

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎傅宣歎曰：「今日-{復}-見武帝之世矣！」

translations.literal: Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates Fu Xuan exclaimed, "Today we again see an age like Emperor Wu's!"
translations.idiomatic: Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates Fu Xuan sighed, "Today we are living again in the age of Emperor Wu!"

sentences.zh: 十二月，壬午朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, new moon of day renwu; there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the new moon of day renwu, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 太傅越以詔書-{徴}-河間王顒爲司徒，顒乃就-{徴}-。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Yue by edict summoned Prince of Hejian Yong as Minister of Education; Yong then accepted the summons.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Yue issued an edict summoning the Prince of Hejian, Sima Yong, to the post of Minister of Education, and Yong complied.

sentences.zh: 南陽王模遣其將梁臣邀之-{於}-新安，車上扼殺之，-{並}-殺其三子。

translations.literal: Prince of Nanyang Mo sent his general Liang Chen to intercept him at Xin'an, strangled him in the carriage, and also killed his three sons.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Nanyang, Sima Mo, sent his general Liang Chen to waylay him at Xin'an, throttled him in his carriage, and killed his three sons as well.

sentences.zh: 辛-{丑}-，以中書監温羨爲左光祿大夫，領司徒；

translations.literal: Day xinchou, Supervisor of the Imperial Secretariat Wen Xian was made Left Minister of the Imperial Household, acting as Minister of Education;
translations.idiomatic: On day xinchou, Wen Xian, supervisor of the imperial secretariat, was appointed Left Minister of the Imperial Household with acting rank as Minister of Education;

sentences.zh: 尚書左-{僕}-射王衍爲司空。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Yan was made Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: and Wang Yan, left vice director of the Masters of Writing, became Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 己酉，葬惠帝-{於}-太陽陵。

translations.literal: Day jiyou, buried Emperor Hui at the Taiyang tomb.
translations.idiomatic: On day jiyou, Emperor Hui was buried at the Taiyang tomb.

sentences.zh: 劉琨至上黨，東燕王騰卽自井陘東下。

translations.literal: Liu Kun reached Shangdang; Prince of Dongyan Teng immediately came east from Jingxing Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun reached Shangdang just as Prince Teng of Dongyan marched east through Jingxing Pass.

sentences.zh: 時并州饑饉，數爲胡寇所掠，郡縣莫能自保。

translations.literal: At that time Bing Province suffered famine; it was repeatedly plundered by Hu raiders; districts and counties could not protect themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Bing Province was then in famine and had been raided again and again by non-Chinese bands; neither district nor county could hold its own.

sentences.zh: 州將田甄、甄弟蘭、任祉、祁濟、李惲、薄盛等及使民萬-{餘}-人，悉隨騰就-{穀}-冀州，號爲「乞活」，所-{餘}-之戸不滿二萬，寇賊縱橫，道路斷塞。

translations.literal: Provincial officers Tian Zhen, Zhen's younger brother Lan, Ren Zhi, Qi Ji, Li Yun, Bo Sheng, and others, together with more than ten thousand dispatched people, all followed Teng to seek grain in Ji Province, calling themselves "those begging to live"; remaining households did not reach twenty thousand; brigands ranged freely; roads were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial commanders Tian Zhen, his brother Lan, Ren Zhi, Qi Ji, Li Yun, Bo Sheng, and others, along with more than ten thousand people the province had sent out, all trailed Teng into Ji Province in search of grain, calling themselves the "Begging-to-Live" band. Fewer than twenty thousand households were left behind; robbers roamed unchecked and the roads were impassable.

sentences.zh: 琨募兵上黨，得五百人，轉鬪而前。

translations.literal: Kun recruited troops at Shangdang, obtained five hundred men, and fought as he advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Kun raised five hundred men at Shangdang and fought his way forward.

sentences.zh: 至晉陽，府寺焚毀，邑野蕭條，琨撫循勞徠，流民稍集。

translations.literal: Reaching Jinyang, government offices were burned down; towns and countryside were desolate; Kun comforted, encouraged, and drew in the weary; displaced people gradually gathered.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Jinyang the government compounds lay in ashes and the countryside was empty. Kun soothed the people, called back the exiles, and refugees slowly returned.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，癸-{丑}-，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, day guichou, general amnesty; era name changed.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on day guichou, there was a general amnesty and the era name was changed.

sentences.zh: 吏部郎周穆，太傅越之姑子也，與其妹夫-{御}-史中丞諸葛玫説越曰：「主上之爲太弟，張方意也。

translations.literal: Lang of the Ministry of Personnel Zhou Mu, a nephew by marriage of Grand Tutor Yue, with his sister's husband Supervisor Imperial Inspecting Censor Zhuge Mei said to Yue, "The sovereign's appointment as Heir Presumptive was Zhang Fang's idea.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Mu, a lang in the Ministry of Personnel and Yue's nephew by marriage, together with his brother-in-law Zhuge Mei, supervisor imperial inspecting censor, told Yue, "The present emperor was made heir presumptive only because Zhang Fang wanted it.

sentences.zh: 淸河王本太子，公宜立之。」

translations.literal: Prince of Qinghe was originally Crown Prince; Your Excellency ought to install him."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qinghe was the rightful crown prince. You ought to restore him."

sentences.zh: 越不許。

translations.literal: Yue did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Yue refused.

sentences.zh: 重言之，越怒，斬之。

translations.literal: When they repeated it, Yue grew angry and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: When they pressed the point, Yue flew into a rage and had them both executed.

sentences.zh: 二月，王彌寇靑、徐二州，自稱-{征}-東大將軍，攻殺二千石。

translations.literal: Second month, Wang Mi raided the two provinces of Qing and Xu, styled himself General Who Campaigns East, and attacked and killed ranked officials at the two-thousand-bushel level.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Wang Mi ravaged Qing and Xu provinces, styled himself General Who Campaigns East, and killed several prefect-level officials.

sentences.zh: 太傅越以公車令東萊鞠羨爲本郡太守，以討彌，彌撃殺之。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Yue made Commandant of the Imperial Chariots Ju Xian of Donglai administrator of his home commandery to attack Mi; Mi attacked and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Yue appointed Ju Xian of Donglai, commandant of the imperial chariots, native administrator of Donglai to suppress Mi, but Mi struck first and killed him.

sentences.zh: 陳敏刑政無章，不爲英俊所附；

translations.literal: Chen Min's punishments and government lacked order; he won no attachment from eminent men;
translations.idiomatic: Chen Min governed without law or measure and won no loyalty from men of talent;

sentences.zh: 子弟凶暴，所在爲患；

translations.literal: his sons and younger brothers were brutal and violent; wherever they went they were a scourge;
translations.idiomatic: his sons and brothers were brutal wherever they went;

sentences.zh: 顧榮、周□等憂之。

translations.literal: Gu Rong, Zhou □, and others were troubled by this.
translations.idiomatic: and Gu Rong, Zhou □, and their circle were deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 廬江内史華譚遺榮等書曰：「陳敏盜-{據}-呉、會，命危朝露。

translations.literal: Interior Minister of Lujiang Hua Tan sent Gu Rong and others a letter saying, "Chen Min has seized Wu and Kuai by robbery; his life hangs like morning dew.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Tan, interior minister of Lujiang, wrote to Gu Rong and the others: "Chen Min holds Wu and Kuai by force; his fate hangs by a thread.

sentences.zh: 諸君或剖符名郡，或列爲近臣，而更辱身-{姦}-人之朝，降節叛逆之黨，不亦羞乎！

translations.literal: You gentlemen either hold investiture in famous commanderies or rank as close ministers, yet you further demean yourselves in a traitor's court and lower your dignity to join a rebel faction — is it not shameful!
translations.idiomatic: Some of you bear seals in renowned commanderies, others serve as the emperor's close attendants, yet you demean yourselves in a traitor's court and bow to rebels — have you no shame!

sentences.zh: 呉武烈父子皆以英傑之-{才}-，繼承大業。

translations.literal: Father and son of Wu the Martial and Fierce all possessed heroic talent and succeeded to the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian and Sun Ce were men of heroic stature who built a great enterprise.

sentences.zh: 今以陳敏凶狡，七弟頑冗，欲躡桓王之髙蹤，蹈大皇之絶軌，遠度諸賢，猶當未許也。

translations.literal: Now with Chen Min's vicious cunning and his seven brothers' stupidity and redundancy, wishing to follow Duke Huan's lofty tracks and tread the Great Sovereign's peerless path — even measuring from afar, you eminent men should still not approve.
translations.idiomatic: Now Chen Min is vicious, his seven brothers are dull and useless, and they dream of matching Duke Huan of Qi and treading in the footsteps of Sun Quan the Great Sovereign — even at a distance, gentlemen like you should refuse such a pretense.

sentences.zh: 皇輿東返，俊彦盈朝，將舉六師以淸建業，諸賢何顏-{復}-見中州之士邪？」

translations.literal: The imperial carriage returns east; outstanding talents fill the court; they will raise six armies to clear Jianye — how can you gentlemen bear to face the gentlemen of the Central Plains again?"
translations.idiomatic: The imperial carriage is returning east, the court is full of able men, and six armies will soon march to cleanse Jianye — how will you face the gentry of the central provinces again?"

sentences.zh: 榮等素有圖敏之心，及得書，甚慚，密遣使報-{征}-東大將軍劉准，使-{發}-兵臨江。

translations.literal: Rong and others had long harbored intent against Min; receiving the letter they were deeply ashamed, secretly sent envoys to report to General Who Campaigns East Liu Zhun, asking him to send troops to the river.
translations.idiomatic: Rong and his allies had long plotted against Min. The letter shamed them into action; they secretly sent word to General Who Campaigns East Liu Zhun asking him to move troops to the river.

sentences.zh: 己爲内應，剪-{髮}-爲信。

translations.literal: They would act as insiders within; cut hair as token of trust.
translations.idiomatic: They would act as his agents inside the city and sent cut locks of hair as proof of their pledge.

sentences.zh: 准遣揚州刺史劉機等出-{歴}-陽討敏。

translations.literal: Zhun sent Governor of Yangzhou Liu Ji and others out from Liyang to attack Min.
translations.idiomatic: Zhun dispatched Liu Ji, governor of Yangzhou, and others from Liyang to attack Min.

sentences.zh: 敏使其弟廣武將軍昶將兵數萬屯烏江，-{歴}-陽太守宏屯牛渚。

translations.literal: Min sent his younger brother General of Guangwu Chang with tens of thousands of troops to encamp at Wujiang; Administrator of Liyang Hong encamped at Niuzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Min sent his brother Chang, general of Guangwu, with tens of thousands of men to hold Wujiang, while Hong, administrator of Liyang, camped at Niuzhu.

sentences.zh: 敏弟處知顧榮等有貳心，勸敏殺之，敏不從。

translations.literal: Min's younger brother Chu knew Gu Rong and others had divided loyalties and urged Min to kill them; Min did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Min's brother Chu saw that Gu Rong and the others were wavering and urged Min to kill them, but Min refused.

sentences.zh: 昶司馬錢廣，周□同郡人也，□密使廣殺昶，因宣言州下已殺敏，敢動者誅三族。

translations.literal: Chang's marshal Qian Guang was from the same commandery as Zhou □; □ secretly had Guang kill Chang, then proclaimed that below the province Min had already been killed — whoever stirred would have three generations executed.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's marshal Qian Guang came from the same commandery as Zhou □. □ secretly ordered Guang to kill Chang, then announced that Min was already dead throughout the province and that anyone who moved would suffer the extermination of three generations.

sentences.zh: 廣勒兵朱雀橋南；

translations.literal: Guang arrayed troops south of the Zhuque Bridge;
translations.idiomatic: Guang drew up his troops south of the Zhuque Bridge;

sentences.zh: 敏遣甘卓討廣，堅甲精兵盡委之。

translations.literal: Min sent Gan Zhuo to attack Guang, entrusting him with all the hard armor and picked troops.
translations.idiomatic: and Min sent Gan Zhuo against him with every suit of heavy armor and elite soldier he had.

sentences.zh: 顧榮慮敏疑之，故往就敏。

translations.literal: Gu Rong feared Min suspected him and therefore went to approach Min.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Rong, afraid Min might suspect him, went in person to see Min.

sentences.zh: 敏曰：「卿當四出鎭衞，豈得就我邪！」

translations.literal: Min said, "You ought to guard on all four sides — how can you come stay by me!"
translations.idiomatic: Min said, "You should be guarding the four quarters — what business have you sitting here beside me!

sentences.zh: 榮乃出，與周□共説甘卓曰：「若江東之事可濟，當共成之。

translations.literal: Rong then went out and, together with Zhou □, jointly urged Gan Zhuo, saying, "If the affairs of Jiangdong can succeed, we ought to accomplish them together.
translations.idiomatic: Rong went out and, with Zhou □, went together to persuade Gan Zhuo: "If we can bring the lower Yangtze enterprise to success, we should finish it together.

sentences.zh: 然卿觀茲事勢，當有濟理不？

translations.literal: Yet when you survey the present situation, is there any reasonable prospect of success?
translations.idiomatic: But look at how matters stand — is there really any chance this can succeed?

sentences.zh: 敏旣常-{才}-，政令反覆，計無所定，其子弟各已驕矜，其敗必矣。

translations.literal: Min has long been mediocre in talent; his government orders shift back and forth and his plans never settle; his sons and younger brothers are already arrogant and self-important — his defeat is certain.
translations.idiomatic: Min has never been more than ordinarily capable; his orders change from day to day and his plans never hold; his sons and brothers are already insufferably proud — he is bound to fall.

sentences.zh: 而吾等安然受其官祿，事敗之日，使江西諸軍函首送洛，題曰『逆賊顧榮、甘卓之首』，此萬世之辱也！」

translations.literal: Yet we calmly accept his salaries and stipends; on the day of defeat, the armies west of the river will pack our heads in boxes and send them to Luoyang, inscribed "Heads of the traitors Gu Rong and Gan Zhuo" — that would be shame for ten thousand generations!"
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile we sit here taking his pay in comfort; when he falls, the armies west of the Yangtze will ship our heads to Luoyang in boxes labeled "Heads of the rebels Gu Rong and Gan Zhuo." That would be an infamy that would never die!

sentences.zh: 卓遂詐稱疾，迎女，斷橋，收船南岸，與□、榮及前-{松}-滋侯相丹楊紀瞻共攻敏。

translations.literal: Zhuo then pretended illness, went to meet his daughter, cut the bridge, gathered boats on the south bank, and together with □, Rong, and the former Marquis of Songsizi, chancellor of Danyang Ji Zhan, jointly attacked Min.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo feigned sickness, fetched his daughter, severed the bridge, and pulled all boats to the south bank; then he joined □, Rong, and Ji Zhan — once Marquis of Songsizi, now chancellor of Danyang — in an attack on Min.

sentences.zh: 敏自帥萬-{餘}-人討卓，軍人隔水語敏衆曰：「本所以戮力陳公者，正以顧丹楊、周安-{豐}-耳；

translations.literal: Min himself led more than ten thousand men to attack Zhuo; soldiers across the water called to Min's host, saying, "The reason we all strained our strength for Lord Chen was precisely Gu of Danyang and Zhou of Anfeng;
translations.idiomatic: Min led more than ten thousand men against Zhuo in person. Soldiers on the far bank shouted to Min's troops: "We threw in our lot with Lord Chen only because of Gu Rong of Danyang and Zhou □ of Anfeng;

sentences.zh: 今皆異矣，汝等何爲！」

translations.literal: now they have all turned — what are you still fighting for!"
translations.idiomatic: and now they have switched sides — why are you still fighting?"

sentences.zh: 敏衆狐疑未決，榮以白羽扇麾之，衆皆潰去。

translations.literal: Min's troops wavered and could not decide; Rong waved a white feather fan at them, and the whole host scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Min's men hung back, uncertain; Rong merely waved a white feather fan, and they broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 敏單騎北走，追獲之-{於}-江乘，歎曰：「諸人誤我，以至今日！」

translations.literal: Min fled north alone on horseback; pursued and captured at Jiangcheng, he sighed and said, "Men have misled me, bringing me to this day!"
translations.idiomatic: Min fled north alone; caught at Jiangcheng, he sighed: "These men have ruined me and brought me to this pass!

sentences.zh: 謂弟處曰：「我負卿，卿不負我！」

translations.literal: He said to his younger brother Chu, "I have failed you; you have not failed me!"
translations.idiomatic: He told his brother Chu, "I wronged you; you did not wrong me."

sentences.zh: 遂斬敏-{於}-建業，夷三族。

translations.literal: He then beheaded Min at Jianye and exterminated three generations of his clan.
translations.idiomatic: Min was executed at Jianye and his clan was wiped out to the third degree.

sentences.zh: -{於}-是會稽等郡盡殺敏諸弟。

translations.literal: Thereupon Kuaiji and other commanderies killed all of Min's younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Kuaiji and the other commanderies then hunted down and killed every one of Min's brothers.

sentences.zh: 時平東將軍周馥代劉准鎭壽春。

translations.literal: At that time General Who Pacifies the East Zhou Fu replaced Liu Zhun as garrison commander at Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Pacifies the East Zhou Fu had replaced Liu Zhun in command at Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 三月，己未朔，馥傳敏首至京師。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the first day of the month (jiwei), Fu forwarded Min's head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jiwei, the new moon, Fu sent Min's head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 詔-{征}-顧榮爲侍中，紀瞻爲尚書郎。

translations.literal: An edict summoned Gu Rong to be Palace Attendant and Ji Zhan to be Master of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: The court summoned Gu Rong as Palace Attendant and appointed Ji Zhan Master of Writing.

sentences.zh: 太傅越-{辟}-周□爲參軍，陸玩爲手彖。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Yue recruited Zhou □ as staff officer and Lu Wan as staff recorder.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Yue took Zhou □ onto his staff as a staff officer and appointed Lu Wan a staff recorder.

sentences.zh: 玩，機之從弟也。

translations.literal: Wan was a younger cousin of Lu Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wan was a younger cousin of the poet Lu Ji.

sentences.zh: 榮等至徐州，聞北方愈亂，疑不進，越與徐州刺史裴盾書曰：「若榮等顧望，以軍禮-{發}-遣！」

translations.literal: When Rong and the others reached Xuzhou and heard that the north was growing still more chaotic, they hesitated and would not advance; Yue wrote to Pei Dun, governor of Xuzhou, saying, "If Rong and the others hang back, dispatch them under military law!"
translations.idiomatic: Rong and his party reached Xuzhou, heard how much worse the north had become, and stalled. Yue wrote Pei Dun, governor of Xuzhou: "If Rong and the rest linger, drive them on under military law!"

sentences.zh: 榮等懼，逃歸。

translations.literal: Rong and the others were afraid and fled home.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Rong and the others slipped away and returned south.

sentences.zh: 盾，楷之兄子，越妃兄也。

translations.literal: Dun was a nephew of Pei Kai and elder brother to Yue's consort.
translations.idiomatic: Dun was Pei Kai's nephew and the elder brother of Yue's wife.

sentences.zh: 西陽夷寇江夏，太守楊鈱請督將議之。

translations.literal: Xiyang barbarians raided Jiangxia; Administrator Yang Qian asked the supervising generals to discuss the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyang tribesmen invaded Jiangxia; Administrator Yang Qian called his commanders in council.

sentences.zh: 諸將爭獻方略，騎督朱伺獨不言。

translations.literal: The generals vied to offer stratagems; only Cavalry Commander Zhu Si kept silent.
translations.idiomatic: Every officer competed to propose plans; only Cavalry Commander Zhu Si said nothing.

sentences.zh: 鈱曰：「朱將軍何以不言？」

translations.literal: Qian said, "General Zhu, why do you not speak?"
translations.idiomatic: Qian asked, "General Zhu, why have you not spoken?"

sentences.zh: 伺曰：「諸人以舌撃賊，伺惟以力耳。」

translations.literal: Si said, "The rest strike at the enemy with their tongues; I rely on force alone."
translations.idiomatic: Si replied, "These men fight the enemy with talk; I fight with force alone."

sentences.zh: 鈱又問：「將軍前-{後}-撃賊，何以常勝？」

translations.literal: Qian asked again, "When you attacked the enemy before and after, why were you always victorious?"
translations.idiomatic: Qian pressed him: "You have beaten the enemy again and again — what is your secret?"

sentences.zh: 伺曰：「兩敵共對，惟當忍之；

translations.literal: Si said, "When two foes face each other, one must only endure;
translations.idiomatic: Si said, "When two enemies stand opposed, the only thing to do is endure;

sentences.zh: 彼不能忍，我能忍，是以勝耳。」

translations.literal: they cannot endure while I can — that is why I win."
translations.idiomatic: they cannot bear it and I can — that is why I win."

sentences.zh: 鈱善之。

translations.literal: Qian approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: Qian was pleased with the answer.

sentences.zh: 詔追-{復}-楊太-{后}-尊號；

translations.literal: An edict restored the honorific title of Empress Dowager Yang;
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored the posthumous honors of Empress Dowager Yang;

sentences.zh: 丁卯，改葬之，諡曰武悼。

translations.literal: on dingmao she was reburied, with the posthumous name Martial and Lamented.
translations.idiomatic: on dingmao she was reinterred under the temple name Martial and Lamented.

sentences.zh: 庚午，立淸河王覃弟豫章王詮爲皇太子。

translations.literal: On gengwu the younger brother of Prince Qinghe Tan, Prince of Yuzhang Quan, was installed as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu Prince Quan of Yuzhang, younger brother of Prince Qinghe Tan, was made heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 辛未，大赦。

translations.literal: On xinwei there was a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei the throne proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 帝親覽大政，留心庶事；

translations.literal: The emperor personally reviewed great affairs of state and attended to common business;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor began to handle major policy himself and took an interest in everyday administration;

sentences.zh: 太傅越不悅，固求出籓。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Yue was displeased and firmly requested to go out to a frontier fief.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Yue was displeased and repeatedly asked to leave the capital for a provincial post.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，越出鎭許昌。

translations.literal: On gengchen Yue went out to garrison Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen Yue withdrew to hold Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 以髙密王略爲-{征}-南大將軍，都督荊州諸軍事，鎭襄陽；

translations.literal: Prince of Gaomi Lue was made General Who Campaigns South, commander of all military affairs in Jing province, and garrisoned at Xiangyang;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Lue of Gaomi was appointed General Who Campaigns South, commander of Jing province forces, with his seat at Xiangyang;

sentences.zh: 南陽王模爲-{征}-西大將軍，都督秦、雍、梁、益四州諸軍事，鎭長安；

translations.literal: Prince of Nanyang Mo was made General Who Campaigns West, commander of all military affairs in the four provinces Qin, Yong, Liang, and Yi, and garrisoned at Chang'an;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Mo of Nanyang became General Who Campaigns West, commanding Qin, Yong, Liang, and Yi, stationed at Chang'an;

sentences.zh: 東燕王騰爲新蔡王，都督司、冀二州諸軍事，仍鎭鄴。

translations.literal: Prince of Dongyan Teng was made Prince of Xincai, commander of all military affairs in the two provinces Si and Ji, and still garrisoned at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Teng of Dongyan was demoted to Prince of Xincai, given command of Si and Ji, and kept his garrison at Ye.

sentences.zh: 公師籓旣死，汲桑逃還苑中，更聚衆劫掠郡縣，自稱大將軍，聲言爲成都王報仇；

translations.literal: After Gongshi Fan died, Ji Sang fled back into the parklands, gathered men again, and plundered commanderies and counties; he styled himself Grand General and proclaimed that he was avenging the Prince of Chengdu;
translations.idiomatic: When Gongshi Fan fell, Ji Sang slipped back into the imperial park, rallied another band, and raided the countryside; calling himself Grand General, he said he was avenging Prince Ying of Chengdu;

sentences.zh: 以石勒爲前驅，所向輒克，署勒掃虜將軍，遂進攻鄴。

translations.literal: he took Shi Le as vanguard; wherever they went they prevailed; he appointed Le General Who Sweeps Away Barbarians, then pressed the attack on Ye.
translations.idiomatic: with Shi Le as his spearhead he swept all before him, made Le General Who Sweeps the Barbarians, and marched on Ye.

sentences.zh: 時鄴中府庫空竭，而新蔡武哀王騰資用甚饒。

translations.literal: At the time the treasuries in Ye were empty, but Prince of Xincai, the Martial and Lamented Teng, was very well supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Ye itself was stripped bare, but Prince Teng of Xincai — posthumously Martial and Lamented — sat on ample stores.

sentences.zh: 騰性吝嗇，無所振惠，臨急，乃賜將士米各數升，帛各丈尺，以是人不爲用。

translations.literal: Teng was by nature stingy and granted no relief; only when crisis came did he bestow on officers and soldiers a few pints of grain each and a foot or so of cloth each — for this reason men would not fight for him.
translations.idiomatic: Teng was miserly and gave nothing away until disaster struck; then he doled out a few pints of grain and a foot of cloth per man — so no one would stand for him.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，桑大破魏郡太守馮-{嵩}-，長驅入鄴，騰輕騎出奔，爲桑將李-{豐}-所殺。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, Sang routed Administrator of Wei commandery Feng Song, drove straight into Ye; Teng fled on light horse and was killed by Sang's officer Li Feng.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer Sang shattered Feng Song, administrator of Wei, stormed Ye, and Teng fled on horseback only to be cut down by Sang's officer Li Feng.

sentences.zh: 桑出成都王穎棺，載之車中，毎事啓而-{後}-行。

translations.literal: Sang brought out the coffin of Prince of Chengdu Ying, loaded it on a cart, and before every action would consult it and only then advance.
translations.idiomatic: Sang exhumed Prince Ying of Chengdu's coffin, carried it in a wagon, and would "consult" the prince before every move.

sentences.zh: 遂燒鄴宮，火旬日不滅；

translations.literal: He then burned the palace at Ye; the fire did not die for ten days;
translations.idiomatic: He burned the Ye palaces; the blaze raged ten days without going out;

sentences.zh: 殺士民萬-{餘}-人，大掠而去。

translations.literal: he killed more than ten thousand gentry and commoners and departed after great plunder.
translations.idiomatic: slaughtered more than ten thousand civilians, and marched off with enormous booty.

sentences.zh: 濟自延津，南撃兗州。

translations.literal: Ji crossed from Yanjin and struck Yanzhou southward.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le crossed the Yellow River at Yanjin and swept south into Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 太傅越大懼，使苟晞及將軍王贊等討之。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Yue was greatly afraid and sent Gou Xi and Generals Wang Zan and others to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Yue, terrified, dispatched Gou Xi, Wang Zan, and others against him.

sentences.zh: 秦州流民鄧定、訇氐等-{據}-成固，寇掠漢中，梁州刺史張殷遣巴西太守張燕討之。

translations.literal: Qin province displaced persons Deng Ding, the Qiang of Hong, and others seized Chenggu, raided and plundered Hanzhong; Inspector of Liang province Zhang Yin sent Administrator of Baxi Zhang Yan to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Displaced people from Qin — Deng Ding, the Hong Qiang, and others — seized Chenggu and ravaged Hanzhong; Zhang Yin, inspector of Liang, sent Zhang Yan, administrator of Baxi, to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 鄧定等饑窘，詐降-{於}-燕，且賂之，燕爲之緩師。

translations.literal: Deng Ding and the others, pressed by hunger, pretended to surrender to Yan and also bribed him; Yan slackened his army on their account.
translations.idiomatic: Starving, Deng Ding's band feigned surrender to Yan and bought him off; Yan eased the siege.

sentences.zh: 定密遣訇氐求救-{於}-成，成主雄遣太尉離、司徒-{雲}-、司空璜將兵二萬救定。

translations.literal: Ding secretly sent the Hong Qiang to seek rescue from Cheng; the lord of Cheng, Xiong, sent Grand Marshal Li, Minister of Works Yun, and Minister of Works Huang with twenty thousand troops to save Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Ding secretly asked the Hong Qiang to call on Cheng; Cheng's ruler Xiong sent Li the Grand Marshal, Yun the Minister of Works, and Huang the Minister of Works with twenty thousand men to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 與燕戰，大破之，張殷及漢中太守杜孟治棄城走。

translations.literal: They fought Yan and routed him; Zhang Yin and Administrator of Hanzhong Du Mengzhi abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: They smashed Yan's force; Zhang Yin and Du Mengzhi, administrator of Hanzhong, abandoned their cities and ran.

sentences.zh: 積十-{餘}-日，離等引還，盡徙漢中民-{於}-蜀。

translations.literal: After more than ten days Li and the others withdrew, moving all the people of Hanzhong into Shu.
translations.idiomatic: After a fortnight Li's army withdrew, deporting the entire population of Hanzhong into Shu.

sentences.zh: 漢中人句方、白落帥吏民還守南鄭。

translations.literal: Ju Fang and Bai Luo of Hanzhong led officials and people back to hold Nanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Ju Fang and Bai Luo in Hanzhong rallied the local gentry and returned to defend Nanzheng.

sentences.zh: 石勒與苟晞等相持-{於}-平原、陽平間，數月，大小三十-{餘}-戰，互有勝負。

translations.literal: Shi Le and Gou Xi and others faced off between Pingyuan and Yangping for months; in large and small engagements more than thirty battles, each side had victories and defeats.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le and Gou Xi grappled for months between Pingyuan and Yangping — thirty-odd clashes in all, with fortunes shifting either way.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，己酉朔，太傅越屯官渡，爲晞聲援。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the first day of the month (jiyou), Grand Tutor Yue encamped at Guandu to support Xi.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on jiyou, the new moon, Grand Tutor Yue camped at Guandu to back Xi.

sentences.zh: 己未，以琅邪王睿爲安東將軍，都督揚州江南諸軍事，假節，鎭建業。

translations.literal: On jiwei Prince of Langye Rui was made General Who Pacifies the East, commander of all military affairs south of the Yangtze in Yang province, with provisional credentials, garrisoning Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei Prince Rui of Langye was named General Who Pacifies the East, given command of Jiangnan in Yang province, full credentials, and a seat at Jianye.

sentences.zh: 八月，己卯朔，苟晞撃汲桑-{於}-東武陽，大破之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the first day of the month (jimao), Gou Xi attacked Ji Sang at Dongwuyang and routed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on jimao, the new moon, Gou Xi struck Ji Sang at Dongwuyang and broke him.

sentences.zh: 桑退保淸淵。

translations.literal: Sang fell back to defend Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Sang withdrew to Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 分荊州、江州八郡爲湘州。

translations.literal: Eight commanderies of Jing and Jiang provinces were carved out as Xiang province.
translations.idiomatic: Eight commanderies from Jing and Jiang were separated to form Xiang province.

sentences.zh: 九月，戊申，琅邪王睿至建業。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on wushen, Prince of Langye Rui reached Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on wushen, Prince Rui of Langye arrived at Jianye.

sentences.zh: 睿以安東司馬王導爲謀主，推心親信，毎事咨焉。

translations.literal: Rui took Eastern Pacification Chief of Staff Wang Dao as his chief strategist, trusting him with open heart and consulting him on every matter.
translations.idiomatic: Rui made Wang Dao, his chief of staff for Eastern Pacification, his chief strategist — trusting him completely and consulting him on everything.

sentences.zh: 睿名論素輕，呉人不附，居久之，士大夫莫有至者，導患之。

translations.literal: Rui's reputation had always been slight; the people of Wu would not attach themselves to him; after he had been there a long time, no gentry came to call; Dao was troubled by this.
translations.idiomatic: Rui's name meant little in the south; the Wu gentry would not rally to him; months passed without a single eminent visitor, to Dao's dismay.

sentences.zh: 會睿出觀禊，導使睿乘肩輿，具威儀，導與諸名勝皆騎從，紀瞻、顧榮等見之驚異，相帥拜-{於}-道左。

translations.literal: When Rui went out to observe the spring purification rites, Dao had Rui ride in a shoulder carriage with full guard of honor; Dao and all the leading figures rode in attendance; Ji Zhan, Gu Rong, and others saw this and were startled; they led one another in bowing by the roadside.
translations.idiomatic: At the spring purification festival Dao put Rui in a curtained palanquin with full escort while he and every local notable rode behind; Ji Zhan, Gu Rong, and the rest were astonished and bowed along the road.

sentences.zh: 導因説睿曰：「顧榮、賀循，此土之望，宜引之以結人心。

translations.literal: Dao then urged Rui, saying, "Gu Rong and He Xun are the pillars of this land; you should draw them in to bind hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Dao told Rui: "Gu Rong and He Xun are the men this country respects — recruit them and you will win hearts.

sentences.zh: 二子旣至，則無不來矣。」

translations.literal: Once those two come, none will fail to come."
translations.idiomatic: Once those two arrive, everyone else will follow."

sentences.zh: 睿乃使導躬造循、榮，二人皆應命而至。

translations.literal: Rui then had Dao go in person to visit Xun and Rong; both men accepted the summons and came.
translations.idiomatic: Rui sent Dao himself to call on Xun and Rong; both answered the summons.

sentences.zh: 以循爲呉國内史；

translations.literal: He made Xun interior minister of Wu;
translations.idiomatic: He appointed He Xun interior minister of Wu;

sentences.zh: 榮爲軍司，加散騎常侍，凡軍府政事，皆與之謀議。

translations.literal: Rong was made army aide-de-camp, with additional appointment as Regular Attendant at the Imperial Library; all military headquarters affairs were deliberated with them.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Rong became army secretary with the added rank of Regular Attendant; every matter of the commandery was settled with their counsel.

sentences.zh: 又以紀瞻爲軍祭酒，卞壺爲從事中郎，周□爲倉曹屬，琅邪劉超爲-{舍}-人，張闓及魯國孔衍爲參軍。

translations.literal: He also made Ji Zhan army libationer, Bian Hu a staff officer, Zhou □ registrar of the granary bureau, Liu Chao of Langye a palace attendant, Zhang Kai and Kong Yan of Lu as staff officers.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Zhan was made army libationer; Bian Hu, a staff officer; Zhou □, registrar; Liu Chao of Langye, palace attendant; Zhang Kai and Kong Yan of Lu, staff officers.

sentences.zh: 壺，粹之子；

translations.literal: Hu was the son of Cui.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Hu was the son of Bian Cui.

sentences.zh: 闓，昭之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Kai was a great-grandson of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kai was a great-grandson of Zhang Zhao.

sentences.zh: 王導説睿：「謙以接士，儉以足用，用淸靜爲政，撫綏新舊。」

translations.literal: Wang Dao urged Rui: "Receive gentlemen with humility, use thrift to make resources suffice, govern with clarity and quiet, and soothe old and new alike."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao counseled him: "Meet men with humility, spend sparingly, rule with calm, and comfort both the old residents and the refugees."

sentences.zh: 故江東歸心焉。

translations.literal: Therefore Jiangdong gave him its hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangdong thereafter gave him its loyalty.

sentences.zh: 睿初至，頗以酒廢事；

translations.literal: When Rui had first arrived, he rather neglected affairs through wine;
translations.idiomatic: Early on Rui neglected government for drink;

sentences.zh: 導以爲言。

translations.literal: Dao spoke to him about it.
translations.idiomatic: Dao remonstrated with him.

sentences.zh: 睿命酌，引觴覆之，-{於}-此遂絶。

translations.literal: Rui ordered wine poured, raised his cup and overturned it, and from that time gave it up entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Rui called for wine, then upended his cup and never drank again.

sentences.zh: 苟晞追撃汲桑，破其八壘，死者萬-{餘}-人。

translations.literal: Gou Xi pursued and attacked Ji Sang, broke eight of his camps, and the dead numbered more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Xi chased Ji Sang, stormed eight camps, and left more than ten thousand dead.

sentences.zh: 桑與石勒收-{餘}-衆，將奔漢，冀州刺史譙國丁紹邀之-{於}-赤橋，又破之。

translations.literal: Sang and Shi Le gathered the remnant host and were about to flee to Han; Ding Shao of Qiaoguo, inspector of Ji province, intercepted them at Chiqiao and defeated them again.
translations.idiomatic: Sang and Shi Le regrouped and headed for the Han state; Ding Shao of Qiaoguo, inspector of Ji, ambushed them at Chiqiao and routed them again.

sentences.zh: 桑奔馬牧，勒奔樂平。

translations.literal: Sang fled to Mumu; Le fled to Leping.
translations.idiomatic: Sang ran to Mumu; Le to Leping.

sentences.zh: 太傅越還許昌，加苟晞撫軍將軍、都督靑、兗諸軍事，丁紹-{寧}-北將軍，監冀州諸軍事，皆假節。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Yue returned to Xuchang; Gou Xi was promoted to General Who Pacifies the Army and commander of all military affairs in Qing and Yan, Ding Shao to General Who Tranquilizes the North, overseeing all military affairs in Ji — all with provisional credentials.
translations.idiomatic: Yue returned to Xuchang, promoted Gou Xi to General Who Pacifies the Army with command of Qing and Yan, and Ding Shao to General Who Tranquilizes the North overseeing Ji — each with full credentials.

sentences.zh: 晞屢破強寇，威名甚盛，善治繁劇，用法嚴峻。

translations.literal: Xi repeatedly defeated powerful bandits; his martial renown was very great; he was skilled at governing complex affairs and applied the law with severity.
translations.idiomatic: Xi had crushed one fierce enemy after another; his fame was immense; he handled tangled affairs with ease and enforced the law ruthlessly.

sentences.zh: 其從母依之，晞奉養甚厚。

translations.literal: His aunt by marriage lived with him, and Xi supported her very generously.
translations.idiomatic: An aunt lived in his household and he maintained her lavishly.

sentences.zh: 從母子求爲將，晞不許，曰：「吾不以王法貸人，將無-{後}-悔邪！」

translations.literal: The aunt's son asked to be made a commander; Xi would not agree and said, "I do not bend the king's law to favor anyone — will you not regret it later!"
translations.idiomatic: Her son asked for a command; Xi refused: "I do not trade away the law for favors — you will regret this!"

sentences.zh: 固求之，晞乃以爲督護；

translations.literal: He pressed the request; Xi then made him a camp protector;
translations.idiomatic: When the youth insisted, Xi made him a camp protector;

sentences.zh: -{後}-犯法，晞杖節斬之，從母叩頭救之，不-{聽}-。

translations.literal: later he violated the law; Xi, staff of authority in hand, beheaded him; his aunt kowtowed to beg for his life, but Xi would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: later the man broke the law; Xi executed him with his credential staff in hand; his aunt kowtowed and pleaded, but Xi would not hear her.

sentences.zh: 旣而素服哭之曰：「殺卿者，兗州刺史；

translations.literal: Afterward he put on plain dress and wept for him, saying, "The one who killed you was the inspector of Yanzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Then he donned mourning white and wept: "The man who killed you was the inspector of Yanzhou;

sentences.zh: 哭弟者，苟道將也。」

translations.literal: the one who weeps for a younger brother is Colonel Gou."
translations.idiomatic: the man who weeps for his brother is Colonel Gou."

sentences.zh: 胡部大張㔨督、馮莫突等，擁衆數千，壁-{於}-上黨，石勒往從之，因説㔨督等曰：「劉單-{于}-舉兵撃晉，部大拒而不從，自度終能獨立乎？」

translations.literal: Grand chieftain of the Hu Zhang Bilidu, Feng Motu, and others held several thousand men and fortified at Shangdang; Shi Le went to join them and urged Bilidu and the rest, saying, "Chanyu Liu has raised troops to strike Jin; the Budu has refused to follow — do you think you can stand alone in the end?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bilidu, grand chieftain of the Hu, Feng Motu, and others held several thousand warriors at Shangdang; Shi Le attached himself to them and argued: "Chanyu Liu is marching against Jin, yet the Budu will not follow — do you imagine you can stand alone?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「不能。」

translations.literal: They said, "We cannot."
translations.idiomatic: We cannot," they said.

sentences.zh: 勒曰：「然則安可不早有所屬！

translations.literal: Le said, "Then how can you fail to attach yourselves early to someone!
translations.idiomatic: Le pressed on: "Then why not choose a master now!

sentences.zh: 今部落皆已受單-{于}-賞募，往往聚議，欲叛部大而歸單-{于}-矣。」

translations.literal: Now the tribes have all accepted the Chanyu's rewards and recruitment; they often gather to discuss betraying the Budu and returning to the Chanyu."
translations.idiomatic: Every clan has taken the Chanyu's pay; men are already plotting to abandon the Budu and go over to Liu."

sentences.zh: 㔨督等以爲然。

translations.literal: Bilidu and the others thought this right.
translations.idiomatic: Bilidu and the rest agreed.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，督等隨勒單騎歸漢，漢王淵署㔨督爲親漢王，莫突爲都督部大，以勒爲輔漢將軍、平晉王，以統之。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Bilidu and the others followed Le on horseback alone back to Han; Han King Yuan appointed Bilidu Prince Who Is Close to Han, Motu commander Budu, and Le Auxiliary Han General and Prince Who Pacifies Jin, to command them.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter Bilidu and his chiefs rode back to Han with Le; Liu Yuan made Bilidu Prince Close-to-Han, Motu commander of the Budu, and Le Auxiliary Han General and Prince Who Pacifies Jin, putting them all under his command.

sentences.zh: 烏桓張伏利度有衆二千，壁-{於}-樂平，淵屢招，不能致。

translations.literal: Wuhuan Zhang Folidu had two thousand men and fortified at Leping; Yuan repeatedly summoned him but could not win him over.
translations.idiomatic: The Wuhuan Zhang Folidu held two thousand men at Leping; Yuan courted him repeatedly without success.

sentences.zh: 勒偽獲罪-{於}-淵，往奔伏利度；

translations.literal: Le pretended to have incurred guilt before Yuan and fled to join Folidu;
translations.idiomatic: Le feigned disgrace at Yuan's court and fled to Folidu;

sentences.zh: 伏利度喜，結爲兄弟，使勒帥諸胡寇掠，所向無前，諸胡畏服。

translations.literal: Folidu was pleased, swore brotherhood with him, and had Le lead the various Hu in raids; wherever they went none could stand before them, and all the Hu feared and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Folidu welcomed him, they became sworn brothers, and Le led the Hu in raids none could stop; every tribe came to fear him.

sentences.zh: 勒知衆心之附己，乃因會執伏利度，謂諸胡曰：「今起大事，我與伏利度誰堪爲主？」

translations.literal: Le knew the hearts of the masses inclined to him; he then seized Folidu at a gathering and said to the various Hu, "Now that we raise a great affair, between Folidu and me who is fit to be leader?
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that the warriors favored him, Le seized Folidu at a feast and asked the chiefs: "If we rise in earnest, who should lead — he or I?"

sentences.zh: 諸胡-{咸}-推勒。

translations.literal: All the Hu unanimously pushed Le.
translations.idiomatic: Every man present acclaimed Le.

sentences.zh: 勒-{於}-是釋伏利度，帥其衆歸漢。

translations.literal: Le thereupon released Folidu and led his followers back to Han.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Le freed Folidu and took his band back to the Han court.

sentences.zh: 淵加勒督山東-{征}-諸軍事，以伏利度之衆配之。

translations.literal: Yuan added Le as commander of all eastern expeditions east of the mountains, assigning Folidu's troops to him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan made Le commander of military affairs east of the mountains and gave him Folidu's force.

sentences.zh: 十一月，戊申朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the first day wushen, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, at the new moon on wushen day, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，以尚書右-{僕}-射和郁爲-{征}-北將軍，鎭鄴。

translations.literal: On jiayin, He Yu, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was made General Who Campaigns North and posted at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin day He Yu, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, became General Who Campaigns North and was stationed at Ye.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，以王衍爲司徒。

translations.literal: On yihai, Wang Yan was made Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai day Wang Yan was appointed Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 衍説太傅越曰：「朝廷危亂，當賴方伯，宜得文武兼資以任之。」

translations.literal: Yan urged Grand Tutor Yue, saying, "The court is in peril and turmoil; we must rely on regional lords — the post should go to one who combines civil and military talent."
translations.idiomatic: “Wang Yan told Yue the court was crumbling and must lean on great regional powers, and needed someone equally adept in civil and martial matters.”

sentences.zh: 乃以弟澄爲荊州都督，族弟敦爲靑州刺史，語之曰：「荊州有江、漢之固，靑州有負海之險，卿二人在外而吾居中，足以爲三窟矣。」

translations.literal: He therefore appointed his younger brother Cheng governor of Jing and his clansman Dun governor of Qing, telling them, "Jing has the Yangzi and Han as ramparts; Qing has the sea at its back. With you two abroad and me at the center, we have our three bolt-holes."
translations.idiomatic: He installed his brother Cheng as Jingzhou governor and his cousin Dun as Qingzhou governor, saying: "Jing is shielded by the Yangzi and Han; Qing rests on the sea. You two abroad and I at court — that is three refuges, enough to survive anything."

sentences.zh: 澄至鎭，以郭舒爲別駕，委以府事。

translations.literal: When Cheng reached his post, he made Guo Shu Registrar and entrusted him with the headquarters affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At his post Cheng made Guo Shu Registrar and delegated all headquarters business to him.

sentences.zh: 澄日夜縱酒，不親庶務，雖寇戎交急，不以爲懷。

translations.literal: Cheng drank day and night and did not attend to routine business; though bandits and aliens pressed hard, he did not care.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng drank round the clock and ignored routine affairs; even as enemies closed in he showed no concern.

sentences.zh: 舒常切諫，以爲宜愛民養兵，保全州境，澄不從。

translations.literal: Shu often remonstrated sharply, urging that he should cherish the people, train troops, and preserve the province; Cheng would not heed.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Shu pleaded repeatedly that he must care for the people, keep the army ready, and hold the province — Cheng refused.

sentences.zh: 十二月，戊寅，乞活田甄、田蘭、薄盛等起兵，爲新蔡王騰報仇，斬汲桑-{於}-樂陵。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on wuyin, Tian Zhen, Tian Lan, Bo Sheng of the Qihuo and others raised troops to avenge Prince of Xincai Teng and beheaded Ji Sang at Leling.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on wuyin, Qihuo leaders Tian Zhen, Tian Lan, and Bo Sheng rose to avenge Prince Teng of Xincai and executed Ji Sang at Leling.

sentences.zh: 棄成都王穎棺-{於}-故井中，穎故臣收葬之。

translations.literal: They cast the coffin of Prince of Chengdu Ying into an old well; Ying's former ministers recovered and buried it.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's coffin was thrown into an abandoned well; his former retainers retrieved it for proper burial.

sentences.zh: 甲午，以前太傅劉實爲太尉，實以老固辭，不許。

translations.literal: On jiawu, former Grand Tutor Liu Shi was made Grand Commandant; Shi pleaded age and firmly declined, but was not allowed.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu day former Grand Tutor Liu Shi was appointed Grand Commandant; citing age he refused firmly and was overruled.

sentences.zh: 庚子，以光祿大夫髙光爲尚書令。

translations.literal: On gengzi, Court Gentleman for the Splendid Gao Guang was made Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi day Gao Guang, Court Gentleman for the Splendid, became Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 前北軍中候呂雍、度支校尉陳顏等，謀立淸河王覃爲太子；

translations.literal: Former Colonel of the North Army Lü Yong, Commissary Officer Chen Yan and others plotted to install Prince of Qinghe Tan as heir apparent;
translations.idiomatic: Lü Yong, former Colonel of the North Army, Chen Yan the commissary officer, and others conspired to make Prince Tan of Qinghe crown prince;

sentences.zh: 事覺，太傅越矯詔囚覃-{於}-金墉城。

translations.literal: When the plot was discovered, Grand Tutor Yue forged an edict and imprisoned Tan in Jincheng fortress.
translations.idiomatic: The plot was exposed; Yue forged an edict and imprisoned Tan in the Jincheng fortress.

sentences.zh: 初，太傅越與苟晞親善，引升堂，結爲兄弟。

translations.literal: Earlier, Grand Tutor Yue had been close to Gou Xi, brought him up to the hall, and sworn brotherhood.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yue had been on intimate terms with Gou Xi — he received him in the hall and they became sworn brothers.

sentences.zh: 司馬潘滔説越曰：「兗州-{衝}-要，魏武以之創業。

translations.literal: Army Aide Pan Tao said to Yue, "Yanzhou is strategic — it was with it that Wei Wu founded his enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Tao, Yue's staff officer, said: "Yanzhou is the hinge of the realm — Cao Cao built his empire from it.

sentences.zh: 苟晞有大-{志}-，非純臣也，久令處之，則患生心腹矣。

translations.literal: Gou Xi has great ambitions and is no pure loyalist; leave him there long and trouble will breed at your very vitals.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Xi is ambitious and no wholehearted loyalist; keep him there and trouble will strike at your heart.

sentences.zh: 若遷-{於}-靑州，厚其名號，晞必悅。

translations.literal: If he is moved to Qingzhou and his title is richly enhanced, Xi will surely be pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Transfer him to Qingzhou with a grand title and he will be satisfied.

sentences.zh: 公自牧兗州，經緯諸夏，籓衞本朝，此所謂爲之-{於}-未亂者也。」

translations.literal: You yourself should pasture Yan, organize All-under-Heaven, and garrison the court — this is what they call acting before disorder arises."
translations.idiomatic: Take Yan yourself, govern the central provinces, and shield the throne — that is acting before chaos sets in."

sentences.zh: 越以爲然。

translations.literal: Yue thought it right.
translations.idiomatic: Yue agreed.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，越自爲丞相，領兗州牧，都督兗、豫、司、冀、幽、并諸軍事。

translations.literal: On guimao, Yue made himself Chancellor, took charge as Governor of Yan, and commanded all military affairs in Yan, Yu, Si, Ji, You, and Bing.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao Yue declared himself Chancellor, took Yan as his own fief, and commanded armies in Yan, Yu, Si, Ji, You, and Bing.

sentences.zh: 以晞爲-{征}-東大將軍、開府儀同三司，加侍中、假節、都督靑州諸軍事，領靑州刺史，封東平郡公。

translations.literal: Gou Xi was made General Who Campaigns East, with the Staff equal to the Three Dukes, added Palace Attendant, provisional credentials, commander of all Qing military affairs, Governor of Qing, and enfeoffed as Duke of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Xi became General Who Campaigns East with Three-Duke honors, Palace Attendant, full credentials, commander of Qing, governor of the province, and Duke of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 越、晞由是有隙。

translations.literal: From this Yue and Xi had a rift.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Yue and Gou Xi were at odds.

sentences.zh: 晞至靑州，以嚴刻立威，日行斬戮，州人謂之「屠伯」。

translations.literal: When Xi reached Qing, he established awe through harsh severity and executed daily; the people of the province called him "the Butcher Lord."
translations.idiomatic: At Qingzhou Xi ruled by terror, ordering executions every day; the people dubbed him "the Butcher Lord."

sentences.zh: 頓丘太守魏植爲流民所逼，衆五六萬，大掠兗州，晞出屯無鹽以討之。

translations.literal: Dunqiu Prefect Wei Zhi was pressed by displaced persons, fifty or sixty thousand strong, who plundered Yan on a great scale; Xi marched out and encamped at Wuyan to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Dunqiu prefect Wei Zhi was overrun by fifty or sixty thousand refugees who ravaged Yan; Xi encamped at Wuyan to attack them.

sentences.zh: 以弟純領靑川，刑殺更甚-{於}-晞。

translations.literal: He had his younger brother Chun hold Qingchuan; executions there were even more severe than Xi's.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Chun held Qingchuan and killed even more freely than Xi.

sentences.zh: 晞討植，破之。

translations.literal: Xi attacked Zhi and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Xi defeated Zhi in battle.

sentences.zh: 初，陽平劉靈，少貧賤，力-{制}-奔牛，走及奔馬，時人雖異之，莫能舉也。

translations.literal: Earlier, Liu Ling of Yangping, poor and lowly in youth, could subdue a running ox by force and outpace a galloping horse; though men marveled, none could raise him up.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ling of Yangping had been born poor; he could wrestle running oxen and outrun horses — people marveled, yet no one advanced him.

sentences.zh: 靈撫膺歎曰：「天乎，何當亂也！」

translations.literal: Ling beat his breast and sighed, "Heaven! When will it come to chaos!
translations.idiomatic: He clutched his chest and cried: "O Heaven — when will the world finally break apart!

sentences.zh: 及公師籓起，靈自稱將軍，寇掠趙、魏。

translations.literal: When the princes and commanderies rose, Ling styled himself general and raided Zhao and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When the princes and regional lords rose in arms, he called himself general and raided Zhao and Wei.

sentences.zh: 會王彌爲苟純所敗，靈亦爲王贊所敗，遂倶遣使降漢。

translations.literal: When Wang Mi was defeated by Gou Chun, Ling was also defeated by Wang Zan; they both then sent envoys to surrender to Han.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mi fell to Gou Chun and Ling to Wang Zan; both sent envoys to surrender to Han.

sentences.zh: 漢拜彌鎭東大將軍、靑徐二州牧、都督縁海諸軍事，封東萊公；

translations.literal: Han appointed Mi General Who Guards the East, Governor of the two provinces Qing and Xu, commander of all coastal military affairs, and enfeoffed him Duke of Donglai;
translations.idiomatic: Han made Mi General Who Guards the East, governor of Qing and Xu, commander of coastal regions, and Duke of Donglai;

sentences.zh: 以靈爲平北將軍。

translations.literal: and Ling was made General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: Ling became General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 李釗至-{寧}-州，州人奉釗領州事。

translations.literal: When Li Zhao reached Ningzhou, the people of the province installed Zhao to head provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhao reached Ningzhou and the locals put him in charge of the province.

sentences.zh: 治中毛孟詣京師，求刺史，累上奏，不見省。

translations.literal: Registrar Mao Meng went to the capital to request a governor; he submitted memorials repeatedly but received no notice.
translations.idiomatic: Registrar Mao Meng went to the capital seeking an appointed governor; his memorials piled up unanswered.

sentences.zh: 孟曰：「君亡親喪，幽閉窮城，萬-{里}-訴哀，精誠無感，生不如死！」

translations.literal: Meng said, "Our lord perished, kin are in mourning, the city is shut in desperate isolation — ten thousand li to plead in grief, yet sincerity moves no one; to live is worse than to die!
translations.idiomatic: Mao Meng cried: "Our lord is dead, kin in mourning, the city besieged — we pleaded across ten thousand li and no one heard us; living is worse than dying!

sentences.zh: 欲自刎，朝廷憐之，以魏興大守王遜爲-{寧}-州刺史，仍詔交州出兵救李釗。

translations.literal: He was about to cut his own throat; the court took pity and made Wang Xun, Grand Warden of Weixing, Governor of Ningzhou, and also ordered Jiaozhou to send troops to rescue Li Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: He was about to kill himself; the court relented, made Wang Xun of Weixing governor of Ningzhou, and ordered Jiaozhou to march to Li Zhao's relief.

sentences.zh: 交州刺史吾彦遣其子咨將兵救之。

translations.literal: Governor of Jiaozhou Wu Yan sent his son Zi with troops to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaozhou governor Wu Yan sent his son Zi with an army to relieve them.

sentences.zh: 慕容廆自稱鮮卑大單-{于}-。

translations.literal: Murong Hui styled himself Grand Chanyu of the Xianbei.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Hui proclaimed himself Grand Chanyu of the Xianbei.

sentences.zh: 拓跋祿官卒，弟猗盧總攝三部，與廆通好。

translations.literal: Tuoba Luguan died; his younger brother Yilu took overall charge of the three divisions and entered friendly relations with Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Luguan died; his brother Yilu took command of all three divisions and allied with Hui.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丙午朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the first day bingwu, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, first month, new moon on bingwu day — solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 丁未，大赦。

translations.literal: On dingwei, a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei day a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 漢王淵遣撫軍將軍聰等十將南-{據}-太行，輔漢將軍石勒等十將東下趙、魏。

translations.literal: Han King Yuan sent Pacifying Army General Cong and nine other generals south to hold the Taihang, and Auxiliary Han General Le and nine other generals east against Zhao and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan sent Cong the Pacifying Army General and nine others south to hold the Taihang, and Le the Auxiliary Han General with nine others east into Zhao and Wei.

sentences.zh: 二月，辛卯，太傅越殺淸河王覃。

translations.literal: In the second month, on xinmao, Grand Tutor Yue killed Prince of Qinghe Tan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on xinmao, Yue executed Prince Tan of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 庚子，石勒寇常山，王浚撃破之。

translations.literal: On gengzi, Shi Le invaded Changshan; Wang Jun struck and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi Shi Le attacked Changshan; Wang Jun routed him.

sentences.zh: 涼州刺史張軌病風，口不能言，使其子茂攝州事。

translations.literal: Governor of Liangzhou Zhang Gui was stricken with wind ailment and could not speak; he had his son Mao administer provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gui, governor of Liang, suffered a stroke and could not speak; his son Mao ran the province.

sentences.zh: 隴西内史晉昌張越，涼州大族，欲逐軌而代之，與其兄酒泉太守鎭及西平太守曹祛，謀遣使詣長安告南陽王模，稱軌廢疾，請以秦州刺史賈龕代之。

translations.literal: Interior Minister of Longxi Zhang Yue of Jinchang, a great clan of Liangzhou, wished to drive out Gui and replace him; with his elder brother Zhen, Grand Warden of Jiuquan, and Cao Qu, Grand Warden of Xiping, he plotted to send envoys to Chang'an to report to Prince of Nanyang Mo that Gui was crippled by illness and to ask that Jia Kan, Governor of Qinzhou, replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue of Jinchang, interior minister of Longxi and a powerful Liang clan, schemed to oust Gui; with his brother Zhen, warden of Jiuquan, and Cao Qu, warden of Xiping, he sent to Chang'an to tell Prince Mo of Nanyang that Gui was incapacitated and to name Qinzhou governor Jia Kan as replacement.

sentences.zh: 龕將受之，其兄讓龕曰：「張涼州一時名士，威著西州，汝何德以代之！」

translations.literal: Kan was about to accept; his elder brother remonstrated with Kan, saying, "Governor Zhang of Liang is a man of renown in his time, his prestige shines in the western provinces — by what virtue do you replace him!
translations.idiomatic: Kan nearly accepted; his elder brother barred him: "Zhang of Liang is a man of standing whose authority fills the west — what merit have you to take his place!

sentences.zh: 龕乃止。

translations.literal: Kan then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Kan relented.

sentences.zh: 鎭、祛上疎，更請刺史，未報；

translations.literal: Zhen and Qu submitted memorials, again requesting a governor; no answer came;
translations.idiomatic: Zhen and Qu petitioned again for a new governor; no reply came;

sentences.zh: 遂移檄廢軌，以軍司杜耽攝州事，使耽表越爲刺史。

translations.literal: they then circulated a proclamation deposing Gui, had Army Aide Du Dan administer provincial affairs, and had Dan memorialize for Yue as governor.
translations.idiomatic: they issued a proclamation deposing Gui, put army aide Du Dan in charge, and had Dan nominate Yue as governor.

sentences.zh: 軌下教，欲避位，歸老宜陽。

translations.literal: Gui issued an order of instruction, wishing to yield his post and retire to old age at Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Gui issued an edict offering to step down and retire to Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 長史王融、參軍孟暢蹋折鎭檄，排閣入言曰：「晉室多故，明公撫-{寧}-西夏，張鎭兄弟敢肆凶逆，當鳴鼓誅之。」

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Wang Rong and Staff Officer Meng Chang trampled and broke Zhen's proclamation, pushed through the gate and said, "The house of Jin has many troubles; my lord has pacified the western Xia — the Zhang brothers of Zhen dare such outrage; we should beat the drums and execute them."
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk Wang Rong and aide Meng Chang stormed in, trampled Zhen's proclamation, and said: "Jin is in turmoil and you have held the west in peace — the Zhang brothers of Zhen have risen in treason; sound the drums and put them to death."

sentences.zh: 遂出，戒嚴。

translations.literal: They then went out and proclaimed martial alert.
translations.idiomatic: They marched out and declared martial law.

sentences.zh: 會軌長子實自京師還，乃以實爲中督護，將兵討鎭。

translations.literal: As it happened Zhang Gui's eldest son Shi returned from the capital; Gui then made Shi Central Commander Who Protects and led troops to attack Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Gui's eldest son Shi had just returned from the capital; Gui made him central protector and sent him against Zhen.

sentences.zh: 遣鎭甥太府主簿令狐亞先往説鎭，爲陳利害，鎭流涕曰：「人誤我！」

translations.literal: He sent Zhen's nephew Chief Clerk of the Grand Treasury Linghu Ya ahead to persuade Zhen, setting forth gain and harm; Zhen wept and said, "Men misled me!
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zhen's nephew Linghu Ya ahead to reason with him; Zhen wept: "I was led astray!

sentences.zh: 乃詣實歸罪。

translations.literal: He then went to Shi to submit his guilt.
translations.idiomatic: He came to Shi to surrender and accept judgment.

sentences.zh: 實南撃曹祛，走之。

translations.literal: Shi struck south against Cao Qu and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Shi marched south, routed Cao Qu, and drove him out.

sentences.zh: 朝廷得鎭、祛疎，以侍中袁瑜爲涼州刺史。

translations.literal: When the court received the memorials of Zhen and Qu, it made Palace Attendant Yuan Yu Governor of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court received Zhen and Qu's petitions and appointed Palace Attendant Yuan Yu governor of Liang.

sentences.zh: 治中楊澹馳詣長安，割耳盤上，訴軌之被誣。

translations.literal: Registrar Yang Dan rode post-haste to Chang'an, cut off his ear and set it on a platter, and pleaded that Gui had been slandered.
translations.idiomatic: Registrar Yang Dan galloped to Chang'an, cut off his ear on a platter, and pleaded that Gui had been falsely accused.

sentences.zh: 南陽王模表請停瑜，武威太守張琠亦上表留軌；

translations.literal: Prince of Nanyang Mo memorialized asking to halt Yuan Yu; Grand Warden of Wuwei Zhang Tian also submitted a memorial to retain Gui;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Mo of Nanyang asked that Yuan Yu's appointment be canceled; Wuwei warden Zhang Tian also petitioned to keep Gui;

sentences.zh: 詔依模所表，且命誅曹祛。

translations.literal: an edict followed Mo's memorial, and also ordered the execution of Cao Qu.
translations.idiomatic: the throne sided with Mo and ordered Cao Qu executed.

sentences.zh: 軌-{於}-是命實帥歩騎三萬討祛，斬之。

translations.literal: Gui thereupon ordered Shi to command thirty thousand foot and horse to attack Qu and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Gui then sent Shi with thirty thousand infantry and cavalry against Qu and had him beheaded.

sentences.zh: 張越奔鄴，涼州乃定。

translations.literal: Zhang Yue fled to Ye; Liangzhou was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue fled to Ye and Liangzhou was pacified.

sentences.zh: 三月，太傅越自許昌徙鎭鄄城。

translations.literal: In the third month, Grand Tutor Yue moved his headquarters from Xuchang to Yancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Yue relocated his seat from Xuchang to Yancheng.

sentences.zh: 王彌收集亡散，兵-{復}-大振。

translations.literal: Wang Mi gathered the scattered and lost; his army again swelled greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mi regathered his scattered forces and his army swelled anew.

sentences.zh: 分遣諸將攻掠靑、徐、兗、豫四州，所過攻陷郡縣，多殺守令，有衆數萬；

translations.literal: He dispatched his generals to attack and plunder the four provinces Qing, Xu, Yan, and Yu; wherever they passed they stormed counties and districts, often killing prefects and magistrates, and had several tens of thousands of men;
translations.idiomatic: He sent generals to ravage Qing, Xu, Yan, and Yu, storming counties, killing officials, until his host numbered tens of thousands;

sentences.zh: 苟晞與之連戰，不能克。

translations.literal: Gou Xi fought him in succession but could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Xi fought him repeatedly without success.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丁亥，彌入許昌。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on dinghai, Mi entered Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on dinghai, Mi took Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 太傅越遣司馬王斌帥甲士五千人入衞京師，張軌亦遣督護北宮純將兵衞京師。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Yue sent Army Aide Wang Bin commanding five thousand armored men to enter and guard the capital; Zhang Gui also sent Protector Beigong Chun with troops to guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yue sent Wang Bin with five thousand armored men to guard Luoyang; Zhang Gui sent Beigong Chun with troops as well.

sentences.zh: 五月，彌入自轘轅，敗官軍-{於}-伊北，京師大震，宮城門晝閉。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Mi entered by the Huanyuan Pass, defeated government troops north of the Yi, the capital was greatly shaken, and the palace gates were shut by day.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Mi came through Huanyuan, routed the imperial army north of the Yi, threw Luoyang into panic, and the palace gates were shut even in daylight.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，彌至洛陽，屯-{於}-津陽門。

translations.literal: On renxu, Mi reached Luoyang and encamped at the Jinyang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu Mi reached Luoyang and camped at the Jinyang Gate.

sentences.zh: 詔以王衍都督-{征}-討諸軍事。

translations.literal: An edict made Wang Yan commander of all punitive military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan was ordered to command all punitive operations.

sentences.zh: 甲子，衍與王斌等出戰，北宮純募勇士百-{餘}-人突陳，彌兵大敗。

translations.literal: On jiazi, Yan and Wang Bin and others went out to battle; Beigong Chun recruited over a hundred stalwarts to charge the formation, and Mi's troops were greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi Yan and Wang Bin led the sortie; Beigong Chun gathered a hundred daredevils to break the line and shattered Mi's army.

sentences.zh: 乙-{丑}-，彌燒建春門而東，衍遣左衞將軍王秉追之，戰-{於}-七-{里}-澗，又敗之。

translations.literal: On yichou, Mi burned the Jianchun Gate and went east; Yan sent Left Guards General Wang Bing in pursuit; they fought at the Qili Ravine and defeated him again.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou Mi burned the Jianchun Gate and fled east; Yan sent Wang Bing in pursuit and beat him again at Qili Ravine.

sentences.zh: 彌走渡河，與王桑自軹關如平陽。

translations.literal: Mi fled across the river; with Wang Sang he went from the Zhi Pass to Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Mi crossed the river and with Wang Sang went through Zhi Pass to Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 漢王淵遣侍中兼-{御}-史大夫郊迎，令曰：「孤親行將軍之館，拂席洗爵，敬待將軍。」

translations.literal: Han King Yuan sent Palace Attendant and concurrent Grand Master of Writing to welcome him in the suburbs, with the order: "I shall myself go to the general's lodge, dust the mat and rinse the goblet, and respectfully await the general."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan sent his chief minister to meet him outside the city with this message: "I shall come to your lodge in person, sweep the mat and rinse the cups, and await you with all honor."

sentences.zh: 及至，拜司隸校尉，加侍中、特進，以桑爲散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he was appointed Director of the Masters of Writing for the Capital Area, added Palace Attendant and Special Advance, and Sang was made Attendant Cavalier.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival Mi was made director of the capital region, Palace Attendant, and Special Advance; Sang became Attendant Cavalier.

sentences.zh: 北宮純等與漢劉聰戰-{於}-河東，敗之。

translations.literal: Beigong Chun and others fought Liu Cong of Han in Hedong and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Beigong Chun and his men fought Liu Cong in Hedong and routed him.

sentences.zh: 詔封張軌西平郡公，軌辭不受。

translations.literal: An edict enfeoffed Zhang Gui as Duke of Xiping; Gui declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gui was offered the dukedom of Xiping and refused.

sentences.zh: 時州郡之使，莫有至者，軌獨遣使貢獻，歳時不絶。

translations.literal: At that time, envoys from provinces and prefectures mostly did not arrive; Gui alone sent envoys with tribute, unbroken year after year.
translations.idiomatic: While other provinces sent no envoys, Gui alone maintained tribute without interruption.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，甲辰，漢王淵寇平陽，太守宋抽棄郡走，河東太守路述戰死；

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on jiachen, Han King Yuan invaded Pingyang; Grand Warden Song Chou abandoned the commandery and fled; Hedong Grand Warden Lu Shu died in battle;
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on jiachen, Liu Yuan attacked Pingyang; prefect Song Chou fled; Hedong prefect Lu Shu died fighting;

sentences.zh: 淵徙都蒲子。

translations.literal: Yuan moved his capital to Puzi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan moved his capital to Puzi.

sentences.zh: 上郡鮮卑陸逐延、氐酋單-{征}--{並}-降-{於}-漢。

translations.literal: Luzzuyan the Xianbei of Shang Commandery and Chief Zheng of the Di both surrendered to Han.
translations.idiomatic: Luzzuyan the Xianbei of Shang and the Di chieftain Zheng both submitted to Han.

sentences.zh: 八月，丁亥，太傅越自鄄城徙屯濮陽；

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on dinghai, Grand Tutor Yue moved his encampment from Yancheng to Puyang;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on dinghai, Yue moved from Yancheng to camp at Puyang;

sentences.zh: 未-{幾}-，又徙屯滎陽。

translations.literal: before long he moved his encampment again to Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly after he shifted camp again to Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 九月，漢王彌、石勒寇鄴，和郁棄城走。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Han King Mi and Shi Le invaded Ye; He Yu abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Wang Mi and Shi Le attacked Ye; He Yu fled the city.

sentences.zh: 詔豫州刺史裴憲屯白馬以拒彌，車騎將軍王堪屯東燕以拒勒，平北將軍曹武屯大陽以備蒲子。

translations.literal: An edict had Governor of Yuzhou Pei Xian encamp at Baima to resist Mi, Cavalry General Wang Kan encamp at Dongyan to resist Le, and General Who Pacifies the North Cao Wu encamp at Dayang to guard against Puzi.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xian of Yuzhou was posted at Baima against Mi, Cavalry General Wang Kan at Dongyan against Le, and Cao Wu the General Who Pacifies the North at Dayang facing Puzi.

sentences.zh: 憲，楷之子也。

translations.literal: Xian was the son of Pei Kai.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xian was Pei Kai's son.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，甲戌，漢王淵卽皇帝位，大赦，改元永鳳。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on jiaxu, Han King Yuan assumed the imperial title, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Yongfeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on jiaxu, Liu Yuan took the imperial title, granted amnesty, and proclaimed the era Yongfeng.

sentences.zh: 十一月，以其子和爲大將軍，聰爲車騎大將軍，族子曜爲龍驤大將軍。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, he made his son He Grand General, Cong Cavalry General, and his clansman son Yao Dragon-soaring General.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he made his son He Grand General, Cong Cavalry General, and clansman Yao Dragon-Soaring General.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，并州刺史劉琨使上黨太守劉惇帥鮮卑攻壺關，漢鎭東將軍綦毋達戰敗亡歸。

translations.literal: On renyin, Governor of Bingzhou Liu Kun had Shangdang Grand Warden Liu Dun lead Xianbei to attack Huguan; Han's General Who Guards the East Qimu Da was defeated and fled home.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin Liu Kun of Bingzhou sent Liu Dun of Shangdang with Xianbei against Huguan; Qimu Da the Han general was beaten and fled.

sentences.zh: 丙午，漢都督中外諸軍事、大司馬、領丞相右賢王宣卒。

translations.literal: On bingwu, Han's commander of all military affairs inside and outside, Grand Marshal, Chancellor concurrent, Right Worthy King Xuan died.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu the Han Right Worthy King Xuan — commander of all armies, Grand Marshal, and concurrent chancellor — died.

sentences.zh: 石勒、劉靈帥衆三萬寇魏郡、汲郡、頓丘，百姓望風降附者五十-{餘}-壘；

translations.literal: Shi Le and Liu Ling commanded thirty thousand men and invaded Wei, Ji, and Dunqiu commanderies; the people, seeing the wind and submitting, yielded over fifty fortified camps;
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le and Liu Ling led thirty thousand against Wei, Ji, and Dunqiu; more than fifty fortified camps surrendered at their approach;

sentences.zh: 皆假壘主將軍、都尉印綬，簡其強壯五萬爲軍士，老弱安堵如故。

translations.literal: all were given provisional General and Commandant seals and ribbons; from the strong they chose fifty thousand as soldiers; the aged and weak were settled in peace as before.
translations.idiomatic: each chief was given general or commandant rank; fifty thousand sturdy men were enlisted while the old and weak were left undisturbed.

sentences.zh: 己酉，勒執魏郡太守王粹-{於}-三-{台}-，殺之。

translations.literal: On jiyou, Le seized Grand Warden of Wei Wang Cui at Santai and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou Le seized Wei prefect Wang Cui at Santai and executed him.

sentences.zh: 十二月，辛未朔，大赦。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the first day xinwei, a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, new moon on xinwei — general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，漢主淵以大將軍和爲大司馬，封梁王；

translations.literal: On yihai, Han Emperor Yuan made Grand General He Grand Marshal and enfeoffed him Prince of Liang;
translations.idiomatic: On yihai Liu Yuan made Grand General He Grand Marshal and Prince of Liang;

sentences.zh: 尚書令歡樂爲大司徒，封陳留王；

translations.literal: Minister over the Masses Huan Le became Grand Minister of Education and was enfeoffed as Prince of Chenliu;
translations.idiomatic: Huan Le, Minister over the Masses, was made Grand Minister of Education and enfeoffed as Prince of Chenliu;

sentences.zh: -{後}-父-{御}-史大夫呼延翼爲大司空，封鴈門郡公；

translations.literal: the Empress's father, Grand Master of Documents Huyan Yi, became Grand Minister of Works and was enfeoffed as Duke of Yanmen commandery;
translations.idiomatic: the empress's father, Grand Master of Documents Huyan Yi, was made Grand Minister of Works and enfeoffed as Duke of Yanmen commandery;

sentences.zh: 宗室以親疎悉封郡縣王，異姓以功伐悉封郡縣公侯。

translations.literal: Members of the imperial clan, according to closeness of kin, were all enfeoffed as princes of commanderies and counties; men of other surnames, according to merit in conquest, were all enfeoffed as dukes and marquises of commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial clan were all enfeoffed as princes of commanderies and counties according to the closeness of their kinship; men of other surnames were all enfeoffed as dukes and marquises of commanderies and counties according to their achievements in war.

sentences.zh: 成尚書令楊褒卒。

translations.literal: Cheng Minister over the Masses Yang Bao died.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Bao, Minister over the Masses of Cheng, died.

sentences.zh: 褒好直言，成主雄初得蜀，用度不足，諸將有以獻金銀得官者，褒諫曰：「陛下設官爵，當網羅天下英豪，何有以官買金邪！」

translations.literal: Bao was fond of blunt speech. When Cheng ruler Xiong first obtained Shu, expenses were insufficient; some generals obtained office by presenting gold and silver. Bao remonstrated, saying, "Your Majesty establishes offices and ranks to gather the realm's heroes—how can there be buying offices with gold!"
translations.idiomatic: Bao loved to speak plainly. When Cheng's ruler Xiong first took Shu, funds ran short; some generals won office by presenting gold and silver. Bao remonstrated, "Your Majesty sets up offices and ranks to gather the realm's heroes—how can offices be bought with gold!"

sentences.zh: 雄謝之。

translations.literal: Xiong apologized to him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong apologized to him.

sentences.zh: 雄嘗醉，推中書令杖太官令，褒進曰：「天子穆穆，諸侯皇皇。

translations.literal: Xiong was once drunk and pushed the Director of the Secretariat to beat the Director of Imperial Cuisine with a staff. Bao advanced and said, "The Son of Heaven is solemn; the feudal lords are august.
translations.idiomatic: Once when Xiong was drunk, he pushed the Director of the Secretariat to beat the Director of Imperial Cuisine with a staff. Bao stepped forward and said, "The Son of Heaven should be solemn; the feudal lords should be august.

sentences.zh: 安有天子而爲酗也！」

translations.literal: How can there be a Son of Heaven who behaves like a drunkard!"
translations.idiomatic: How can a Son of Heaven behave like a drunkard!"

sentences.zh: 雄慚而止。

translations.literal: Xiong was ashamed and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed, Xiong stopped.

sentences.zh: 成平寇將軍李鳳屯晉壽，屢寇漢中，漢中民東走荊沔。

translations.literal: Cheng General Who Pacifies Bandits Li Feng was encamped at Jinshou and repeatedly raided Hanzhong; the people of Hanzhong fled east to Jing and Mian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Feng, Cheng's General Who Pacifies Bandits, was encamped at Jinshou and repeatedly raided Hanzhong; the people of Hanzhong fled east toward Jing and Mian.

sentences.zh: 詔以張光爲梁州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Zhang Guang as Inspector of Liang province.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Zhang Guang inspector of Liang province.

sentences.zh: 荊州寇盜不禁，詔起劉璠爲順陽刺史，江、漢間翕然歸之。

translations.literal: Banditry in Jing province could not be suppressed; an edict recalled Liu Fan as Inspector of Shunyang, and the region between the Jiang and Han submitted to him in unanimity.
translations.idiomatic: Banditry in Jing province could not be checked; an edict recalled Liu Fan as inspector of Shunyang, and the lands between the Jiang and Han turned to him as one.
